title: Disposable, miniature internal optical ignition source for ammunition application
abstract: An ammunition cartridge for a gun is optically initiated by a mechanism wholly within the cartridge case itself. The case has as optical primer initiation means producing light fluence to ignite a primer, which ignited primer may in turn ignite into a flashtube, and which ignited flashtube may in turn ignite a bed of propellant in said cartridge. The optical primer initiation means may be an LED, a laser diode, a VCSEL, or some other light emitting device in general. The cartridge optically initiated primer package is so sized and made electrically and mechanically seamlessly physically compatible with current ammunition cartridges such that these new cartridges are completely interchangeable. If the cartridge primer initiation means is of a percussion type, the cartridge is adapted to include an in-line piezoelectric crystal so that electrical power will be generated when the cartridge assembly is struck by a firing pin during percussion type operations; the power is then used to initiate the light emitting device.

title: Electronic fire control system and methods of operating the same
abstract: The present disclosure provides systems and techniques that can be implemented in a gun, such as an electromechanical gun. The gun may charge a capacitor bank, identify a trigger break based on an output generated by a trigger sensor, and transmit a signal based on the trigger break. Transmitting the signal may result in the capacitor bank discharging electric charge such that electric current is directed at an actuator mechanism so as to cause displacement of the actuator mechanism, and the displacement of the actuator mechanism may result in the propulsion of a projectile through a barrel of the gun. The gun may determine that a projectile has been fired based on an output of an accelerometer or a gyroscope, and the gun may recharge the capacitor bank in response to determining that the projectile has been fired.

title: Firearm ammunition availability detection system
abstract: A linear encoder may be used to accurately determine a number of cartridges within a magazine. Further, using a set of magnetic sensors within a buffer tube of a firearm, it is possible to determine whether a cartridge is loaded within a chamber of the weapon and/or whether the firearm is jammed. The determination of cartridges within the magazine in conjunction with the determination of whether a cartridge is in a chamber of a firearm can give a user an accurate ammunition count. Further, the use of the linear encoder makes it possible to accurately determine the cartridge count when different cartridges are loaded into the magazine or when the magazine degrades in quality over time. abstract: [Problem] To provide a firearm control device that can accurately identify a firearm using a magnetic induction coefficient and tightens firearm control. abstract: High pressure is established in an annular reservoir 13 by feeding compressed air in through a port 30. The pulling plate is pulled, the pulling plate drives the reset spring to move towards one end, the reset spring is stretched to deform, meanwhile, the pulling plate drives the sliding rod to move towards one end, the sliding rod drives the clamping piece to move towards one end, a gun is placed into an inner cavity of the positioning hole, the gun is supported through the supporting block, and the pulling plate is loosened, so that the gun is clamped. title: Fast action shock invariant magnetic actuator for firearms
abstract: An electromagnetic actuator includes characteristics of very fast actuation, shock invariant design, and compact size. The actuator may be controlled via a small low voltage power source such as a battery and simple switching logic. Such characteristics are ideally suited for incorporating the actuator into the firing mechanism of a firearm, which are subjected to drop tests to confirm the firearm will not discharge in the absence of trigger pull. Very fast snap-like action is attained by balancing the magnetic forces of two opposing permanent magnets around a stationary yoke and rotating member to create three circulating magnetic flux circuits. A central electromagnet coil amplifies the magnetic flux of one side of the rotating member or the other depending on the power source actuation polarity, thereby creating two possible snap-like actuation positions. The actuator is usable in firing mechanism release or enabling/disabling applications, and interfacing with other type mechanical linkages.

title: "MILES" transceiver display controller unit
abstract: A transmitter and receiver for "MILES" type systems is in a pistol type configuration, and is provided with a display, to indicate the mode of the controller unit, as well as the specific MILES codes which are transmitted or received. title: Determining the far field pressure signatures of air-gun arrays
abstract: An improved method is developed for the purpose of determining the far field pressure signature radiated by a marine seismic source which consists of an array of n air-guns. The improved method involves the measurement of the pressure field in the vicinity of each air-gun by n independent calibrated hydrophones with known positions when all the air-guns are fired individually and simultaneously. The far field pressure signature of the marine seismic source is obtained by ghosting and summing the recorded near field pressure signatures when all the air-guns are fired simultaneously afier removing the contributions from the neighbouring air-guns and the sea surface from the output of each near field hydrophone. The new method differs from the so-called notional source signatures method (US Patent No. 4,868,794) in that it does not involve the formation and solution of n simultaneous equations, which may give rise to instibility problem, and it requires a knowledge of the distance of each hydrophone from the air-gun immediately below it only but not its distances from the neighbouring air-guns and consequently there is no need to calculate the air-bubbles rise velocities and the relative horizontal velocities. One important feature of the new method is that the near field pressure signatures, obtained when all the air-guns are fired individually, are used to calculate not only the geometry of the air-gun-hydrophone system but also the depth of each air-gun and consequently, the depth transducers normally used for determining the depths of the air-guns are not required.

title: Fluidic-electric switch and safety, arming and detonating system using same
abstract: A fluidic safety, arming and detonating system for use in a weapon-carrying missile whose power output is controlled by a fluidic-electric switch. The system's operation is based on two external environmental signatures plus two internal fluidic signatures. The two external environmental signatures, which are prerequisite to subsequent operation of the system, are provided by combustion gases during ignition of the missile and by ram air after lift-off. The two internal fluidic signatures, which are required to arm and detonate the explosive carried by the missile, are provided by the fluidic-electric switch actuated and controlled by two preset fluidic timers, each of which comprises an oscillator coupled with a binary counter. The two timers turn the fluidic-electric switch first ON, which arms the firing circuit, then OFF, which triggers the firing circuit to detonate the explosive.

title: Indexing system to aid in the installation of a telescopic sight on a firearm
abstract: A feature or provision specifically to aid in aligning the vertical and horizontal reticules with respect to the vertical and horizontal axes of the bore during the installation of a telescopic sight (scope) on a firearm which includes at least one mounting boss for securing the telescopic sight. This feature also provides a means of verification that the installed position has not changed during use, and a reference which will allow the scope to be returned to its original calibrated position should it need to be temporarily removed from its mount. This feature is an indexing system. It consists of markings on the scope body, which, when aligned with corresponding marks on the mounting hardware provide a quick, accurate, inexpensive, simple, and intuitive method of properly aligning the scope's vertical and horizontal axes with those of the firearm's bore during installation; and verification of that alignment thereafter without the use of accessory apparatus. It overcomes numerous limitations of the prior art. It has universal application to most currently used mounting system designs. This feature is integral to the scope and mounting system, and therefore does not require any external fixture or attachment. An optional additional feature provides a reference for use in positioning the scope for proper eye relief.

title: Integrated flash hider for small arms suppressors
abstract: A flash hider is configured to reduce a firearm's visible signature. The flash hider extends along a central axis from a proximal end to a distal end. The proximal end defines a central opening to an expanding central volume of a first flash hider portion. One or more outer volumes are located radially outside of the central volume and can be part of first and/or second flash hider portions. When the outer volumes are part of the first flash hider portion, the outer volumes can communicate with the central volume. Optionally, a second flash hider portion includes one or more gas passageways located radially outside of the central volume. For example, gas passageways are interspersed circumferentially with outer volumes of the first flash hider portion, where the gas passageways are isolated from first flash hider portion and receive gas flows via vent openings in the outer wall.

title: Light Gas Gun
abstract: An improved light gas gun launches a projectile in a light gas atmosphere as it travels through a frictionless barrel to achieve high muzzle velocities, decreased acoustic signatures, and increased ranges. The light gas atmosphere is introduced by a purge valve prior to firing or by a muzzle valve that holds a positive light gas pressure on the barrel and breech. The muzzle valve also routes the majority of propellant gases through a suppression canister, reducing the light gas gun's acoustic signature. The frictionless barrel uses light gas propellant routed through gas bearings to keep the projectile centered in the barrel and preclude the projectile from contacting the barrel walls, eliminating barrel wear.

title: Method and device for simulating firing
abstract: The invention relates to a method for simulating the firing of a tubular weapon, according to which the trigger on the tubular weapon is actuated whereby emitting a first laser beam composed of laser pulses in order to attain wide ranges of fire. The trajectory of the fired virtual shot is calculated, and the deviations of the trajectory from the target bearing are continuously determined at the time at which the shot is fired. The first laser beam is slued according to the trajectory deviations, the operating time of the laser pulses of the first laser beam that are reflected by the target is measured, and the distance from the target is determined from this measurement. In order to determine this distance from the target, the e.g. flight time of the fired virtual shot is calculated and compared with the time that has elapsed since the time at which the shot is fired till the time at which the reflected laser pulses are received. In the instance of congruence within a range of tolerance, a second laser beam composed of coded laser pulses is emitted in the direction of emission last assumed by the first laser beam. The second laser beam is received at the target and is calculated there from the position of the detector, which receives the laser beam and which is located at the target, and from the information which concerns damage caused by the hit and which is conveyed using the coding.

The coiled tubing is connected with a hydraulic sand blasting perforating spray gun, then the hydraulic sand blasting perforating spray gun descends into the shaft and extends into an inner cavity of an underground prefabricated throttler lock cylinder, so that high-speed sand-containing fluid in the hydraulic sand blasting perforating spray gun penetrates through a prefabricated throttler air faucet body, the structure of a prefabricated throttler throttling and blocking the shaft is damaged, and meanwhile a working shaft structure and a productionpipe column are not damaged. By spraying the high-pressure high-speed sand-containing fluid in a short time, a gas production channel is opened, so that the production time for stopping due to fishing, grinding and milling operation is greatly shortened, the production is recovered in the shortest time, the yield loss is reduced to the minimum, the risk is controllable, the construction operationcost is low, the long-term production effect of a constructed gas well is good, the application range is wide, a well depth structure of the 3.5-inch tubing-free well completion is also suitable, andthe method is a very effective solution in the aspect of solving the problem that the shaft is blocked by a failure prefabricated throttler.

abstract: A safety device for use with a toy guns, less-lethal guns (such as non- powdered guns) and lethal guns detects motion of the gun, and causes light emitting diodes or other light sources incorporated into the gun to prominently flash. abstract: The invention discloses a diagonal orthogonality construction method for a large-span steel box girder in a complex traffic environment. abstract: An orientation verification tool permits an operator to confirm an orientation of one or more perforating charges in a perforating gun assembly when the perforating charges are not readily visible for inspection. title: Portable apparatus and method for testing and certification of laser-based speed measuring devices
abstract: A portable test and certification unit for laser-based speed measuring devices (e.g., traffic laser guns) is provided. The test and certification unit is capable of performing manual, semi-automatic and automatic measurements on laser guns, ensuring no “missed” steps in the certification process. The unit is optionally supported by a general-purpose digital computer such as a “PC,” which may, in turn, record test results and print certification documents. The test and certification unit allows for fast and accurate certification of laser guns in a laboratory or in the field by operators of only minimal technical skill, thereby saving expense and time, as laser guns no longer must be removed from vehicles and/or shipped to a remote certification facility.

title: Reduced firing signature weapon cartridge
abstract: A reduced signature weapon cartridge is provided which, when fired, produces little or no muzzle blast or noise signature. In particular, a reduced signature weapon cartridge of the present invention comprises a movable piston disposed within the cartridge, disposed in between the high pressure chamber and the projectile. When fired, propellant gases rapidly force the piston forward within the cartridge case, thereby launching the projectile at a subsonic velocity, thereby eliminating the conventional noise signature associated with supersonic velocities. Thereafter, the propellant gases are slowly released from the cartridge case via perforations formed within the piston, grooves formed in the periphery of the piston, or via a gap between the piston and cartridge wall, thereby reducing or eliminating the conventional muzzle blast.

title: Safety magazine with adapter
abstract: Safety magazines used to secure weapons against unauthorised use are disadvantageously specifically designed to fit one category of magazine well. The aim of the invention is to overcome this disadvantage. By combining a safety magazine with a laterally protruding adapter, a category of larger magazine wells can be secured, when the adapter is mounted, while a category of smaller magazine wells can be secured, when the adapter is removed. The more versatile usability of the safety magazine with associated adapter allows at least 50% of the acquisition costs of an additional, larger or smaller safety magazine to be saved. The economically valuable advantage thus obtained offers each user an outstanding product with significantly reduced costs, which allows weapons to be reliably secured for transport and/or against unauthorised use, even with different magazine wells.

title: Sound suppressor for a firearm
abstract: A sound suppressor for a firearm with a high rate of fire, such as a machine gun, conceals the location of the firearm during heavy use by rapidly dissipating heat through a foamed graphite sleeve. A sound suppressing baffle core is coaxially located within a tubular housing having flared ends extending beyond the core. An inlet nozzle and exit plate close the ends of the suppressor and are held in place with threaded collars. The terminal portions of the collars are beveled, as are the corresponding terminal portions of the nozzle and end plate, and are used to capture the flared portions of the ends of the tubular housing. Diagonally opposing recesses in the collars enable their removal with a spanner wrench, along with the other components for maintenance and replacement. The suppressor lasts longer and has a less visible heat signature used in sustained fire on a machine gun.

title: Spectroscopy for gunshot residue analysis
abstract: The present invention relates to a method of detecting inorganic gunshot residue (GSR) particles. Also disclosed is a method of detecting gunshot residue particles. The method includes providing a sample comprising gunshot residue, subjecting the sample to spectroscopic analysis to produce a spectroscopic signature for the sample, where the spectroscopic signature spans a range of wavenumbers, creating one or more spectroscopic maps from the spectroscopic signature for the sample, where each different spectroscopic map is for a different wavenumber, and identifying gunshot residue particles based on the one or more spectroscopic maps for the sample.

abstract: An external lock apparatus for a gun includes a gun receptacle. The gun receptacle is configured to receive a portion of the gun. The external lock further includes an interference member. The interference member is configured to engage with the gun such that the gun cannot be removed from the gun receptacle and the gun cannot fire when the portion of the gun is received within the gun receptacle and the external lock is in the LOCKED position. title: Target system for laser marksmanship training devices
abstract: A target system for laser marksmanship training devices is comprised of one or more photodetectors mounted on a target and sensitive to one or more pulses of the operating wavelength of a laser beam simulating the projectile of a weapon. An amplifier increases the power output of the photodetectors, and a frequency selective transducer is operated from the amplified output of the photodetectors. The transducer is attached and acoustically coupled to the target and produces a vibration signature simulating the vibration characteristics of a weapon-fired projectile striking the target. A microphone sensitive to the vibration signature of the transducer is acoustically coupled to the target, and a drive mechanism lowers the target out of the field of view of the weapon when the microphone receives a hit-indicating vibration signature from the transducer. In a preferred embodiment the laser pulses include a code sequence identification of the weapon being fired and the amplifier includes a decoder for the pulse code sequence. The decoder includes a dual signal threshold level comparator in which a pulse signal level exceeding the first threshold level is established for a man target, and a pulse signal level exceeding the second threshold level is established for a vehicle target whereby the transducer is energized to initiate lowering of the target.

title: Automobile charging pile identity recognition device based on fingerprints
abstract: The utility model discloses an automobile charging pile identity recognition device based on fingerprints. A fingerprint collector is connected with a charging gun body through a cross screw, a physical key is connected with a lock catch through elastic plastic, a limiting pin is located below the physical key, one end of an integrated controller is connected with the fingerprint collector through a data line, and the other end of the integrated controller is connected with the limiting pin through a wire; the central processing unit is connected with the power supply controller through a CAN bus, and the groove is formed in the upper edge of the inner wall of the charging gun socket. When the charging pile needs to be used, the fingerprint collector obtains fingerprint information, and the integrated controller matches the fingerprint information with a fingerprint information base stored in the integrated controller to identify whether the identity of an operator is valid or not. If the identity is valid, the limiting pin is driven to move through an electric signal, so that the physical key can be manually pressed down to unlock the lock catch to take down the charging gun, and the central processing unit sends an instruction to enable the power supply controller to start working after receiving valid information; and if the identity is invalid, the limiting pin limits the movement of the physical key below the physical key, so that the charging gun cannot be taken down.

abstract: A handheld counter-unmanned aerial system (100) for neutralising aerial targets under non-stabilised conditions is disclosed. A launcher unit (102) having a trigger subunit (102A) and a munition interface (102B) fires an anti-UAS grenade (104) selectable from grenade types having different terminal effects. A launcher-mounted fire control system (FCS) (106) detects and continuously tracks the target, automatically identifies the loaded grenade type via the munition interface (102B), selects a corresponding engagement model, and computes a predicted intercept point at which the grenade (104) produces a terminal effect in proximity to the target without direct impact. The fire control system (106) generates a firing authorization signal when engagement validity parameters, including track confidence and target position, are satisfied. A trigger block module (TBM) (108) between the trigger subunit (102A) and the fire control system (106) blocks firing until the firing authorization signal is received, providing closed-loop, human-in-the-loop predictive interception.

title: Management control of assets
abstract: This invention concerns a computerised identity matching management process for regulating the issue of, or the return of, secure assets. The process for regulating the issue of secure assets comprises a step of identifying an asset having a unique classification identifier. The management computer responding to the request by returning a message to the capture apparatus, the message containing a unique code and receipt of the message containing the code at the capture apparatus causing initiation of the capture process. The capture apparatus encoding a captured biometric representative of the issuer of the asset or representative of the receiver of the asset with the code. title: System and method for detecting and responding to a threat in or around a facility
abstract: A system for detecting and mitigating a threat in or around a facility is disclosed. In one embodiment, the system comprises a sensor or receiver configured to detect a biometric marker, such as an iris scan, fingerprint, voice pattern, or facial pattern, and comparing those markers to a database of biometric markers to determine if a match exists. Alternatively, or additionally, the system is configured to detect an anomaly in the background environment of the facility by measuring a variety of variables, such as temperature, pressure, noise-levels, radiation levels, densities, and magnetic fields, and comparing those variables to predetermined threshold values to determine if an anomaly exists. Source 11 delivers a single positive pulse to FF10, thus triggering it to its high current condition so that the output terminal which is normally at- 18 volts becomes less negative. The trunk associated with stage S9, i.e. trunk No. 9, is thus chosen. On the relapse of armature 221, relay 13 falls away, thus disabling B10 and B1, and allowing pulses from the continuouslyrunning source 12 to pass via gate 14 (Fig. 5) to inputs of C1 to C10 and to the output circuit 15. Gate C9 is enabled (FF9 set) and consequently the first pulse passes via C9 to set FF8, and to the output circuit 15. FF8 resets FF9 and enables C8, so that the second pulse passes via C8 to set FF7. The remaining stages operate sequentially in like manner, stages S8 to S1 controlling the sending of eight pulses and OFL that of the ninth. With OFL set, the gate 14 is disabled to stop the supply of pulses from source 12. All trunks busy.-In this case all the gates B1 to B10 are enabled and FF10 to FF1 are operated in succession, followed by OFL which gives an overflow indication to the output circuit 15 over a front contact of relay 13. Second embodiment-different trunks available in differing order for different demands.-In Figs. 6-8 which illustrate this embodiment, a normally closed (break) contact of a relay is shown as a single short line perpendicular to a conductor, and a normally open (make) contact as an X crossing the conductor. There are eleven stages SO-S9 and OFL, of which S0 S1, S9, and OFL only are shown. Each of the ten trunks in the group is associated with one of the contacts TR0 to TR9, the contact being normal (closed) when the trunk is idle, and open when it is busy. Assuming that contact 201 is closed, VG0 pulls up and allots T3, T2, T1, T0, T9 and T8 to stages SO to S5, respectively. The gates BO-B9 (Fig. 12) are normally enabled but those associated with busy trunks are now inhibited by ground extended to their C terminals. FF1 therefore remains set. With FF1 set, positive potential is thus extended over a front VGO contact to operate TSA2 which locks up, indicating that the selected trunk is No. 2. The operation of this relay provides an additional inhibiting ground to TSS1, inhibits all ten gates BO-B9, operates relay TSAK, and enables gates TSR and RI7. Relay TSAK disconnects the relays TSAOTSA9 from network 18, but TSA2 remains locked up. The next pulse from source 11 passes via amplifier TSRA, gates TRI, TCK1 (FF1 set) and amplifier TSRB to the reset terminals CR of TREF, TSK, OFL and FFOFF9, thus inter alia resetting FF1. With RI7 enabled, FF7 is set, thus disabling TCK2 and TCK4 and enabling TCK1 and TCK3, so that the fourth pulse passes from TRE through TCK3 to set TSK which enables the gate TSKA in the outpulsing chain. The next pulse therefore passes via TSKA and the enabled gate CD7 (FF7 set) to set FF8, subsequent pulses setting FF9 and DFL, whereupon OFLA is disabled to prevent further pulses being sent. title: High-spraying construction equipment and method for auxiliary cutting of mechanical arm
abstract: The invention discloses a high-spraying construction device and method for auxiliary cutting of a mechanical arm. The equipment comprises a long spiral drilling machine, a high-pressure guniting system, a long spiral drill rod, an integrated mechanical arm, a same-side multi-nozzle drill bit and an intelligent control system. The mechanical arm main body can stretch along the sliding rail, and the stretching direction is consistent with the nozzle and points to the fore drilling. The intelligent control system monitors the lifting resistance of the drill rod or the parameters of the power head in real time, and automatically stops lifting and withdraws the mechanical arm when the drill rod meets the resistance. The construction steps comprise parameter matching, site preparation, hole drilling, mechanical arm unfolding, jet cutting operation, synchronous quality verification, exception handling and cyclic transition. The wall body lap joint quality is verified by monitoring the driving current or torque, and the lifting and the retracting of the mechanical arm are automatically stopped when the wall body lap joint quality meets resistance. The invention realizes real-time verification of lap joint quality by cooperative operation of mechanical cutting and high-pressure spraying, and solves the problem of poor lap joint reliability of the traditional high-pressure spraying process.

In general, a desired frequency is selected or detected from a number of frequencies present by a heterodyne method. The wanted carrier frequency (N) along with any other frequencies present is combined with a marker frequency (T) in a modulator M. The resultant intermediate frequencies (N-T and others) are applied to either a low-pass filter LPF or an intermediate frequency filter IFA and a detector D which responds only to a standard intermediate frequency (n). Components of the system not specifically mentioned. herein are denoted by symbols M for modulator D for detector IFA and LFA for intermediate and low-frequency amplifiers LPF and BPF for low-pass and band-pass filters. In the example described, separate " go " and " return " co-axial cables are used but a single cable may be used for both directions. title: Intelligent security camera
abstract: Intelligent security cameras provide a solution for burglary and involve an intelligent detection system that employs computer vision, loT, and real-time alerts. Using a Raspberry Pi, the system detects intrusions in two stages by capturing real-time streams from the connected camera. In the first stage, the system registers known faces and recognizes known individuals, thereby reducing false alarms. If a stranger is captured, the recognition of the stranger activates the second stage, where the model is trained to use object recognition to identify unwanted activities such as forcibly entering a door by applying body pressure, picking a lock, hammering a lock, prying a door with a crowbar, breaking with heavy rods. The moment the above actions are detected, the Raspberry Pi responds and triggers two responses simultaneously. First, a control signal is sent to the ESP32 loT microcontroller, which ensures the door is locked immediately from the inside. Second, the user receives an SMS with the live video footage of the scenario, sent through the API. The real-time video footage greatly enhances the integrated approach and ensures that home burglary attempts are proactively dealt with, providing instant user notification, automated security reinforcement, and real-time action recognition to greatly improve home security.

The method comprises the following steps: extracting a current target charge and discharge working mode of a power battery model and a plurality of target charge and discharge influence parameters in the target charge and discharge working mode; establishing a target charging and discharging test working condition corresponding to the target charging and discharging working mode; enabling the test platform to simulate a target charging and discharging working mode and a target charging and discharging test working condition of the power battery model; and by using a target charge-discharge test project corresponding to the target charge-discharge working mode, verifying a target charge-discharge remaining time speculation result corresponding to the target charge-discharge test project and fed back by the battery management system to obtain a corresponding precision verification result. Through the battery charging and discharging time test platform, the estimation precision of the battery relation system on the charging and discharging remaining time is verified, and the estimation precision of the charging and discharging remaining time is improved.

title: Method and system for aerial patrol
abstract: Provided is a method for air patrol comprising the steps of: - determining a patrol route for at least one aircraft apparatus; - directing at least one aircraft apparatus along a predetermined route and, obtaining aerial image data of a terrain with reference to the coordinates and time of image acquisition; - processing, while in flight, image data using a pre-trained machine learning algorithm; - performing, using a machine learning algorithm, image segmentation, pattern recognition and classification of recognized objects along a predetermined patrol route; - identifying at least one type of incident and forming an incident log entry; - verifying at least one of the identified incidents; - transmitting, while in flight, incident log entries to the information and analytical platform server. The technical result is increased efficiency and speed of identifying incidents during aerial patrol, reduced traffic transmission and load on the data transmission network.

title: Method for a two-stage authorization of a charging process on a charging post
abstract: The method according to the invention for a two-stage authorization of a charging process ensures a largely user action-free method, by means of which the personal authorization of a charging post user is carried out in a first step in order to release a charging cable and the authorization to release a charging process is carried out on the basis of a vehicle-side authorization verification received via the connected charging cable in a second step. In the first step, an end terminal-side authorization verification transmitted by a mobile terminal designed as a smart watch for example is received by a control device paired with the charging post. The first personal authorization of the charging post user is checked on the basis of the end terminal-side authorization verification without requiring any action by the charging post user. The charging cable is released upon a given first authorization. In a second step, the vehicle-side authorization verification is received and checked after the vehicle is connected to the charging cable, whereupon in the event of a positive result of the check, a second authorization is carried out followed by a release of the charging process.

abstract: The invention discloses a mistake-proof power transmission system, and relates to the technical field of power management. The system further comprises a label which is arranged on the knife switch, an identification device, a controller, a wireless communication device and a prompting device which are arranged on the brake pull rod, and an identification module. The identification device is device used for identifying the identity of the knife switch by scanning the label, is connected with the controller and communicates with the controller in a one-way mode. The controller is connected to the server through the wireless communication device and communicates with the server in a two-way mode. The controller is connectedwith the prompting device and communicates with the prompting device in a one-way mode. The identification module is used for acquiring the identity information of the knife switch sent by the identification device, comparing the identity information with knife switch information in an operation ticket to obtain a matching result and displaying the matching result through the prompting device. title: Network verification of user equipment (ue) identifier request made by edge client
abstract: Embodiments include methods for a client (e.g., EEC) of an edge data network coupled to a communication network. title: Non-ink-overflow surface coating method for fingerprint chip surface coating
abstract: The invention discloses a non-ink-overflow surface coating method for a fingerprint chip surface coating. The method comprises the following steps that a preset number of openings are prepared on a silk-screen printing screen plate through photosensitive glue, wherein the size of each opening is the same as the size of a fingerprint chip; a preset number of the fingerprint chips are placed in a groove in a printing jig, so as to enable the fingerprint chips to correspond to the openings in the silk-screen printing screen plate; first ink is poured into one end of the silk-screen printing screen plate, a scraper plate is used for scraping on the silk-screen printing screen plate, so as to enable the first ink on the silk-screen printing screen plate to enter the openings formed by the photosensitive glue, and thus the first ink is printed on the surface of each fingerprint chip; the fingerprint chips with the first ink printed on the surfaces is baked in an oven at a first preset temperature for a first preset time period, and then the fingerprint chips is cooled. According to the method, the production cost is reduced, and the diversification of the surface coatings of the fingerprint chips can be realized.

title: Portable laser marking device developed for use in aesthetic surgery
abstract: Portable laser marking device designed for genital aesthetic surgery procedures (gender reassignment surgeries, labia minoraplasty, labia majoraplasty, vaginoplasty, hudoplasty, perinoplasty), Freya Approach Technique supports the application of surgical techniques such as labiaplasty. This technology provides the opportunity to simulate the preoperative golden ratio of the patient's external genital area. This method, which is inspired by the mathematical principles of Fibonacci series, enables more precise markings during surgical intervention and more consistent obtaining of desired aesthetic results. It also offers a personalized aesthetic look to each patient and has the potential to provide high sexual satisfaction by reducing post-surgical complications. This finding guides the surgical team during surgery using VR goggles and laser marking to determine the outer genital anatomy. This technology increases the satisfaction of the patients and optimizes the healing processes by providing more accurate, precise and successful results in genital aesthetic surgery operations based on the fact that every fingerprint is unique and every genital area is unique.

title: Provider-independent hierarchical constraint enforcement architecture for artificial intelligence systems
abstract: A hierarchical constraint enforcement architecture for artificial intelligence systems addresses failures of contractual AI safety governance—including circumvention through provider substitution and erosion through ad-hoc model retraining—by enforcing safety constraints at the deploying entity's own architecture layer, independently of any technology provider. A Constraint Enforcement Layer interposed between an AI processing pipeline and an action execution interface implements three tiers: inviolable constraints cryptographically signed at build time and verified at runtime regardless of provider identity; governance-modifiable constraints subject to authenticated authorization, compatibility validation, and immutable audit records; and operational constraints adjustable within governance-defined bounds. The layer evaluates all proposed actions before execution, maintains deployer-owned persistent state, and persists through provider substitution including government-directed substitution. Applicable across military decision support, clinical AI, large language models, autonomous vehicles, fleet systems, personal assistant operations, executive decision support, regulated communications compliance, patient health advocacy, and governance-as-a-service middleware.

title: Selective pruning of partially conflicting offline digital value objects by steady state transition and canonical local reconstruction method and system
abstract: The invention concerns the protection of the non-conflict section within the secure processing element in the event that only a certain part of a digital value object that can be transferred offline is subject to a dispute of understanding. The secure process element holds the object that contains the root object commitment, proof of descent, value coverage identifier, digital value quantity, and a separate offline authorization capacity. After verifying the conflict section certificate signed by the consensus node, the partial intersection between the object's scope and the quarantine scope is determined. The quarantine area is removed from the object area and the conflict-free residual area is converted into deterministic canonical sub-scopes. While the old object is invalidated with a stable state transition, recovery objects are created for sub-scopes; that transition prevents old and new objects from being simultaneously available after energy or operation interruption. The digital value and offline authorization capacity protections are verified. title: Tapuwise Artificial Intelligence Supported, Ad-Free, Optimized Real Estate Matching, Title Deed Conveyance and Digital Process Management System
abstract: Tapuwise consists of client applications (web/mobile), a backend that works with micro-service architecture, machine learning (ML) servers, and a third-party integration layer. The system simultaneously transmits selfie, ID and title deed documents received from users to official registry systems, and securely authenticates with JSON Web Token (JWT) and OAuth 2.0. Validated data is fed into a hybrid matching engine that combines gradient-boosting, deep learning, and k-nearest neighbor (k-NN) algorithms. The match score is calculated in the range 0-100, with mutual requests above the threshold scheduled to be scheduled for end-to-end encrypted (E2EE) messaging and calendar synchronization. If the appointment is not made, automatic penalty accrual is made over the smart contract (blockchain optional). If the seller chooses a guaranteed sale option, the automatic valuation (AVM) module identifies the price with data and the property is listed with 30% discount by the system; selling within 30 days The real estate transaction platform supported by artificial intelligence, working with verified user data, without ads and digital matching based real estate transaction platform This invention is related to a digital platform that works with artificial intelligence, completely unannounced, and has a double-sided verification system used in real estate buying-selling and leasing processes. It is aimed at a technology that matches the parties in a safe, fast and transparent manner and that concludes the whole process in a digital environment, without the need for human mediation in real estate transactions. Technical Field: Invention is included in the field of real estate technologies (proptech), artificial intelligence supported matching systems, document verification infrastructure and digital transaction platforms. Technical Problems: In the current real estate market, real estate transactions are largely dependent on intermediary persons or companies (real estate agents). This situation: ? Asymmetry of information,? To price uncertainty,? Lack of confidence,? To high service commissions,? It causes a waste of time. In addition, traditional methods, the verification of documents such as title deed and identity is based on manual processes and error-prone. Since the matching process usually works on a ad-based basis, the optimal harmony between the targeted parties cannot be achieved. The goal? Match vendors, buyers, tenants and homeowners to AI-powered algorithms in non-advertised environment,? Enable digital verification of documents (title deeds, ID, selfie) using API and 3rd party systems,? Complete the real estate transactions digitally within 30 days at the latest? To increase the trust between the parties and speed up the process with its fixed, transparent and automatic pricing structure. Solution Path / Technical Specifications: 1. User Verification: Identity, selfie and title deed documents are requested from each user registered on the platform. These documents are verified via the Webtapu API or 3rd party integration systems (example: Apsiyon). 2. AI Mapping: Parameters such as user profiles, property values, locations, price sensitivities, rental/sales preferences are evaluated by AI algorithm. Parties are notified to the system according to the optimum match. 3. Ad-Free Transaction Infrastructure: No ads are opened on the platform. Parties can only negotiate with counterparties that are guided by the system and meet the criteria. Thus, information confidentiality is protected. 4. title: Telecommunication system,in particular telephone system
abstract: 1,187,488. Telecommunication systems; multiplex pulse signalling. INTERNATIONAL STANDARD ELECTRIC CORP. 25 Oct., 1967, No. 48466/67. Headings H4K and H4L. A telecommunication system comprises stations SS, Fig. 1, distributed round a looped unidirectional transmission line LL time division multiplexed from a timing station TS, a calling station being able to seize a free channel for a connection and circulate a code identifying the wanted station. The system employs pulse code modulation with 32 eight bit channels one of which is used for synchronization. During the synch channel the timing station TS, Fig. 3, breaks the loop at A 3 , A 4 to connect a pattern generator PG to one end of the loop and a resistor R to the other end. The synch pattern is all ones. For the 31 channels other than the synch channel a register records idle/busy states. The switches A 3 , A 4 , close to complete the loop for busy channels. Channels occupied with speech have nought in the first bit position while channels occupied with supervisory signals have one in the first bit position. In idle channels the loop is broken and the generator PG injects the code one followed by all noughts. Idle channels are detected by empty channel detector ECD. For calls going outside the loop the timing station has an outgoing number detector OND which connects a channel to a buffer BUF by way of switches A 8 , A 9 . Calls incoming to the loop are detected by IND, the timing station connecting the buffer BUF in a free channel over switches A 8 , A 9 . Synchronization between the framing of signals sent from the timing station and those received after the delay consequent on one circuit of the loop is effected by a variable delay D adjusted frame by frame as described later with reference to Fig. 10. Station equipment, Fig. 2, comprises a microphone and transmitter with associated decoder and coder which can be connected by switches A 1 , A 2 into one limb of the loop as a receive channel and the other limb of the loop as a send channel. With the handset onhook a station number detector SND looks out for the code identifying the station. Should the station code be received a ringing tone generator and bell are activated, the timing circuits detecting the calling channel to operate switches A 1 , A 2 so as to relay a ringing tone code to the calling station. To originate a call the off-hook condition connects up free channel detector ECD which seizes the first channel containing the code 10000000 and operates switches A 1 and A 2 accordingly. The failure of the code 10000000 to complete the loop and return to the timing station signals the timing station that the channel has been seized so that switches A 3 , A 4 can be operated to close the loop. The code of the wanted station is produced by a called number generator CNG, described later with reference to Fig. 8. If the wanted station is idle it responds to the code to break the loop and return ringing tone code in the calling channel. If the station is busy the loop is not so broken and the wanted number code will circuit the loop and be detected at the calling station. Synchronizing station clocks.-A master clock MC divides the bit rate by 16 to obtain channel widths and by 256 to obtain frame lengths. The bit rate is obtained from a free running multivibrator triggered by bit pulses on the line LL. As seen in Fig. 5 the station clock MC produces a synch pulse of the same duration as the synch channel on LL. The synch pulse leading edge sets bi-stable B5/1 to gate the line LL to a ¸ 8 counter. If the synch pulse is in synchronism with the synch channel eight consecutive ones are received and the bi-stable B5/1 is reset; a bi-stable B5/2 in a carry over circuit also being reset. If the synch pulse is not in synchronism with the synch channel the first appearing nought from the line LL resets the counter over inverter 15/1 and B5/1 is not reset from the counter. In case the failure to receive the synch code from LL is due to a transmission fault the carry over circuit responds to the trailing edge of the synch pulse from MC to reset B5/1 and set B5/2, an inhibit circuit H5/2 being open so long as B5/2 is reset and the ¸ 8 counter gives no output. If, however, at the next attempt to match the synch pulse with the synch channel, the ¸ 8 counter fails to find the synch code, the bi-stable B5/1 is not reset by the trailing edge of the synch pulse as B5/2 is set. B5/1 stays set, therefore, while ¸ 8 counter scans a frame in search of the synch code. When the code is found the ¸ 8 counter sets MC to its all ones synch pulse state, sets B5/2, and resets B5/1. Seizure of free channels.-A stepping register SR6/1, Fig. 6, displays and circulates eight consecutive bits from the line LL. Whenever the eight bits complete a channel a sample pulse primes AND gate G6/1. The first bit of each PCM signalling code in a channel is always a one; the corresponding stage of SR6/1 being connected as a direct input to G6/1. When the station handset is off-hook all other stages of the register are connected over inverters to G6/1. When the code marking an idle channel appears gate G6/1 opens to produce pulse P1. A bi-stable B6/1 is set to inhibit the sample pulses at H6/1 and prevent seizure of more than one channel. The pulse P1 gates the master clock MC to a set of bi-stables which record the identity of the seized channel. With the bi-stables set, whenever the clock reaches the position of the seized channel, a pulse is gated to operate station loop contacts A1, A2 (see Fig. 7, not shown). Ringing of wanted station.-With the handset on-hook at a station the register SR6/1 of Fig. 6 is connected to the inverters only in respect of those stages for which a nought appears in the station's code. If a calling station circulates the code, the gate G6/1 opens to produce the pulse P1 at the called station where the channel identity is recorded and loop contacts A 1 , A 2 , operated each time the channel reappears. With the handset on-hook the pulse P1 also triggers the bell and the ringing tone generator RTG. Station key set and connection of busy tone.- While the number of a wanted station could be set up on a decimal keyset and a conversion be made to the corresponding PCM code, the key set shown in Fig. 8 sets up the PCM code direct. As for signals other than speech the first digit in each channel is always a one, the key set has seven keys each of which can set up the corresponding stage of the stepping register SR8/1. The eighth stage of SR8/1 is automatically set up as a one and is read out to line first in the channel seized by a calling station as indicated by gate G8/10. The key settings are read into the register over gates G8/1 to G8/7 and also prime gates G8/11 to G8/17 which latter set of gates open together if the keyed code reappears in the register as read in serially from the line LL. If the code reappears persistently it means that the called station is busy, as it has not responded and broken the loop in the seized channel, and the output of gate G8/8 sets a bi-stable B8/1 to connect busy tone from ENG. If the code does not reappear in the next occurrence of the channel its absence may be the result of propagation time or mutilation and because of this a two-stage counter B8/2, B8/3 is stepped once each frame in the absence of the code until three absences have been detected after which the called station is presumed to be idle, G8/10 closes and the register SR8/1 is stopped. Synchronizing incoming and outgoing sides of timing station.-This involves insertion in the loop of a variable delay in order to make the propagation time round the loop equal an integral number of frame lengths. As shown in Fig. 10 a fixed fraction of the required delay is provided by D10 from which the bit stream on the loop is passed to a stepping register SR10/2 to be tapped off from the stage that introduces the required extra delay. Such tapping is effected by means of one of the gates G10/11 to G10/15 as primed by one of the bi-stables B10/1 to B10/5. One of the bi-stables B10/1 to B10/15 is set according to the distance travelled by a synch pulse PIN, derived from the synch channel by detector SD and stepped along register SR10/1, before the appearance of a synch pulse PREF derived in the timing station. As the pulse PIN may overlap two stages of register SR10/1 the consequent operation of two bi-stables B10/1 to B10/5 will not result in the opening of two gates G10/11 to G10/15 if the dotted line connections are made between bistables and gates. The variable delay is described and claimed in Specification 1,187,489. Multiple loop systems.-Provided the number of loops is small the timing stations of each loop may be connected into a super trunk loop, Fig. 11 (not shown). Otherwise the buffer outlets from the timing station of each loop may be terminated at a central switching station, Fig. 12 (not shown). Provided traffic is light loops may be connected to two other loops to form chains, Fig. 13 (not shown).(From GB1187488 A)

title: Whole-process wholesale tracing method and system for edible agricultural products based on business interior
abstract: An in-growth traceability system for wholesale market business of edible agricultural products. The system acquires original data from a plurality of service data sources, extracts a preset associated identification field group, generates matching confidence through multidimensional combination comparison, automatically judges and associates the matching confidence to the same batch of goods data, and generates a traceable electronic file from entering to selling. The system multiplexes the business data naturally generated in daily operation, and does not require additional entry for traceability purposes. The batch identity is locked by the space-time anchor point of the entrance certificate and the digital fingerprint, and the going tracing is realized by the closed loop of the sales record data. The system automatically optimizes the matching rules based on the historical matching results and the manual review records. When goods flow across markets, the system automatically associates source batches to form a nationwide continuous traceability chain. title: A Mobile Application System That Provides Competitive Bid Generation and Process Control Through User-Defined Demands
abstract: This invention relates to a mobile application-based client-server system in which the product or service needs defined by users are recorded in the system as a demand data object, vendors produce competitive offers based on the said demand data object, and the demand relationship is technically managed by temporal and situational control mechanisms. Within the scope of the invention, the critical parameters such as the budget, time interval, location and scope of the request following the request creation are fixed with a time-based locking mechanism after a short and predefined correction period following the moment of request creation and made unchangeable until certain periods or technical conditions are realized. Thus, all offers produced by sellers are linked to a single and unchanging demand version, ensuring that the offer-demand relationship can be tracked in deterministic form. In addition, the demand lifecycle is managed by a non-reversible state machine logic between predefined technical situations such as creation, locked publication, bid collection, evaluation and conclusion, and a return to previous states after certain stages is technically blocked by the server. All critical operations such as demand generation, locking, bid production and status transitions are recorded with time stamps, increasing the controllability and traceability of the system. Symbols on a proof sheet 16 (Fig. 1) are recognized by means of a continuous rotating disc 19 which bears on it a circumferential row of characters corresponding to those to be found on the proof sheet. These characters are dark on a light background but the reverse arrangement is possible. Light from a source 10 projects the image of a character on to the proof sheet and light received by a photo-electric cell 18 is a maximum when the two characters are the same. When this occurs a gas-filled relay 30 (Fig. 3) is triggered to print a code 38 corresponding to the character recognized on a photographic strip 35. In order that the same amount of light may be passed by each character on the disc a second translucent portion 24 (Fig. 2) is provided whose area is an inverse function of that associated with the symbol 22. A reflecting baffle 26 is provided to mask areas of the proof sheet adjacent the character being recognised and the baffle may be partly masked by an adjustable reflecting shutter 27 which may cut off the image 29 of " make weight " 24 to take account of different paper. When thyratron 30 fires to print the code 38 on the photographic tape it operates relay 31 to cut off the anode supply to the thyratron to terminate the firing and to energize magnetic clutch 39 which is held energized by a second winding of relay 31 until the circuit of this winding is opened once per rotation of a circuit breaker 42 connected to the proof carriage. The amount of movement given to the proof carriage is varied according to the period for which the clutch is energized by rotating switch 32 which connects a number of resistors 40 successively in series with the clutch according to the size of the character printed to step the proof carriage on an appropriate amount. If the proof carriage moves continuously it may be geared to advance during each revolution of the forme carriage, the formes being spaced progressively farther apart. The photo-cell may be connected to the gas-filled tubes through amplifier stages which may operate as the critical stage to detect the amplitude of the signal from the photo-cell instead of the gas-filled tube. To avoid integration of the signal, the photo-cell should be directly coupled to the first stage. A separate flash tube may be used for the photographic printing instead of tube 30. A system using both positive and negative forme symbols may be used having two photo-cells arranged in a bridge or with an output arranged to cut off two triode valves having a common anode resistance across which is a relay stage.

abstract: This invention discloses an advanced acoustic source localization system featuring a unique three-dimensional microphone array arrangement for enhanced accuracy. The 7-sensor array acquires wavefront data simultaneously, enabling accurate bearing calculations and AoA computation in both azimuthal and elevation planes. Operating standalone, the system estimates geo-coordinates locally without remote servers, reducing infrastructure dependence. Optionally, it leverages networks for increased accuracy from remote servers. Offering improved precision, situational awareness, and resilience in complex environments, this system represents a significant advancement over existing single-plane AoA or remote server-based solutions.

abstract: An AI and IoT integrated maritime security platform (OCEANGUARD) with cyber-physical resilience is disclosed. The system integrates heterogeneous IoT security devices (drug testers, chemical analyzers, 3D scanners, X-ray systems), unmanned surveillance assets (autonomous drones with 45-minute endurance, USVs with 24-hour patrol capability), environmental sensors, and AI-driven cybersecurity modules with edge computing infrastructure featuring NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin (275 TOPS) or Google Edge TPU processors for sub-100ms threat detection. A centralized cloud platform employs Vision Transformers (99.2% accuracy), multi-modal fusion networks, and predictive analytics for comprehensive threat analysis. The platform implements zero-trust architecture with quantum-resistant encryption (CRYSTALSKyber/Dilithium), AI-based intrusion detection (<0.1% false negatives), and automated threat response. Federated learning with differential privacy (ε=1.0) and blockchain-secured gradients enables privacy preserving model improvement across multiple ports. Environmental monitoring ensures IMO 2025 compliance with real-time alerts. A digital twin with 5-second synchronization enables scenario planning. The system achieves ≥99% threat detection accuracy, ≥75% inspection time reduction, ≥20% energy savings through predictive maintenance, and 99.99% uptime. Industrial applications include seaports, border checkpoints, offshore platforms, and critical infrastructure, addressing the USD 15 billion maritime AI market by 2030.

Once overlapped the artificial intelligent technique is used to segregate the target sheet into two main categories namely one with distinct marking for each shoot that tallies the total number of markings on the target sheet and total number of shoots. The other is where there is a difference in count clearly implying multiple shoots on same spot for which the system performs image processing for the target sheet before and after each shoot as recorded earlier and finally subjects to colour based scoring using the fuzzy inference engine.

title: An isolation and security system for use in multi-tenant container orchestration
abstract: The invention relates to an isolation and security system running on a server for use in multi-tenant container orchestration. The system of the invention aims to improve security and efficiency by providing isolated network, storage, and control plane environments for each tenant on multi-tenant container orchestration platforms. In this context, network isolation is achieved by using tenant-specific network overlay protocols, unique VXLAN Network Identifier (VNI), distributed routing mechanisms and network policy engine. Complete storage isolation and performance continuity are ensured through separate storage pools, encryption keys, and a storage QoS manager, for each tenant. Control plane isolation is supported by tenant-specific schedulers, admission controllers, and API endpoints, thus, an independent and secure management is offered. Tenant management processes are made efficient with automatic onboarding, dynamic resource allocation, and isolation verifier, and security is guaranteed. Isolated monitoring and log management are carried out with metric aggregators, log managers and anomaly detection engines, and the data integrity and security are guaranteed throughout the system in line with the principle of zero trust architecture.

title: Analytical call distributor device.
abstract: 1374821 Automatic exchange systems COMPAGNIE INDUSTRIELLE DES TELECOMMUNICATIONS CIT-ALCATEL 31 Dec 1971 [31 Dec 1970] 61027/71 Heading H4K In a semi automatic exchange incoming calls are categorized in terms of the junction on which they arrive and are distributed to operators partly in accordance with the category and partly in accordance with their waiting time. The junctions JR (Fig. 1) are monitored on a cyclic basis by a logic LJR in conjunction with a last look memory M having a compartment for each junctor and also a compartment for each operator TO. The latter are cyclically scannable for call distributing purposes by logic LO. Data concerning a call via a junction is amassed in memory and in addition is displayed at an operator position allocated to the call. Data transmission to the operators is effected over a common bus OV in the manner described in Specification 1,355,547. The call distributer DA monitors the logic circuit outputs so as to determine a new call and to allocate thereto a least-busy operator. The call distributer is illustrated in some detail in Figure 2. Essentially is analyses all call data incoming thereto by means of device AA so as to allot a "call-type" code thereto, which code involves the identity of the junction and the "call category" i.e. the nature of the calling subscriber line viz. non fee paying. The operators are each allocated (except in emergency overload) to a particular call-type. The latter always includes more than one call category. The operation of the distributer takes place in a number of phases during the first of which #1 the junctions are scanned in turn (c.f. Specification 1,355,547), the results of scanning are passed to AA over inputs I1, I2 and the resultant code is entered into one of registers RC1, RC2. As each junction is scanned, an indication of the time for which it has been waiting (that is of course only if it is a calling junction) is entered over I3 into one of registers RT1, RT2. The choice of registers is governed by a two step counter CR1 which is stepped on only if (a) an operator is available to handle the call as defined by the particular code allotted thereto (b) phase #1 is present and (c) the new waiting time on I3 exceeds the previous waiting time present in RT1 or RT2 (comparator C1 determines (c)). Thus if the new time is longer it is entered into that one of RT1 and RT2 which was previously empty and the other one having emptied itself of the preceding longest time awaits the entry of a newer longest time. It will be noted that if RT accepts a new longest time, the code of the junction to which it relates is simultaneously entered in an RC register. When all the junctions have been scanned, phase #2 is started during which the code finally set in RC is sent to the operator logic circuit LO so that a hunt may be made through memory to locate the operator denoted by a tag marking who last handled a call having this code. This operator marking serves to denote the point, in the group of operators able to handle calls having the particular code, at which a search for a least busy operator should start. During phase #3, the degree of business of each of the operators within the group is fed via I4 into registers RG. These operate under the control of two step counter CR2 in a similar manner to RT and CR1 so that at the end of the cycle, the least degree of business (but not the identity) of the least busy operator is present in RG. When the cycle ends as denoted by a return to the tag marked operator, the mark is expunged and phase #4 commences during which each operator's business is compared with that recorded in RG. When the first operator who is not busier than that recorded is reached gate P3 is enabled to permit the operator logic LO to mark her position over the common operator data bus and also to enter her identity into store RI. Phase #5 commences wherein all the junctions carrying the particular code, which is still stored in RC, are tested for waiting time so that the one having the longest time as denoted by a comparison with the time stored in RT is selected by the opening of gate P4. The junction identity is passed to the preselected operator and her identity is gated out of store RI and entered into the memory compartment associated with the junction. The distributer resets and a new cycle of operations commences. The full cycle should take 100 msces., if this is exceeded timer OT times out to advance the phase sequences. Overload in the sense of calls waiting longer than a preset period are denoted by the illumination of a lamp ES on a supervisor's panel. She may initiate a hunt, over manual swtch CM, for those calls of a particular category that are experiencing the overload so that they can be dealt with immediately.(From GB1374821 A)

title: Apparatus and method for field-deployable detection of firearm discharge residues
abstract: The present disclosure relates to apparatus and methods for field-deployable detection of firearm discharge residues. The apparatus (102) includes a pulsed laser source (104) emitting optical pulses at a blue wavelength within an optical transmission window of injection-molded polymer material, generating plasma emission light upon irradiation of the biological surface. A transmission diffraction grating (106), formed entirely in injection-molded polymer material, disperses the plasma emission light onto a linear image sensor (108), both positioned within a snap-fit optical housing assembly (110) having molded alignment features. A hardware processor (110) receives intensity values from the linear image sensor 108, maps them to wavelength positions generating a wavelength-resolved intensity profile, and compares the profile against stored reference signatures of firearm discharge residue constituents. A wireless communication transceiver (112) transmits a residue detection signal to an external computing device, which renders a determination of presence or absence of firearm discharge residues.

title: Apparatus for automatically processing and printing the content and format of a text
abstract: 1410353 Text processing ING C OLIVETTI & C SpA 25 Sept 1972 [29 Sept 1971 19 April 1972 14 July 1972] 44238/72 Headings G4H and G4C In a text processing system for preparing and revising multi-line printed texts, lines of text information entered manually are stored on a record medium, and are printed together with identifications of their storage addresses in visual association with the printed lines, manually-operable line searching means permitting a desired address on the record medium to be accessed after which text information can be entered manually thereinto. As disclosed, a central unit having a core memory and processing circuitry and controlled by a programme selected by one of two keyboards from a magnetic tape loop in a cartridge tape memory and read into the core memory in order to control the central unit, can be interrupted by the tape memory, a typewriter (to which one of the keyboards belongs) or a console (to which the other keyboard belongs) for data transfer and execution of functions ordered from the keyboards. The identity of the programme selected by the operator is typed out. The tape loop has N + I tracks, N of which are data tracks each having a sequence of data blocks separated by gaps. Each data block can hold the characters for one line of print, the address within the track of the next block for this text (see below), a constant for track selection, the identity of the cartridge, the number of characters that the line can contain (selectable by the operator), the actual number of characters in the line, the code(s) of function(s) to be carried out on the line (e.g. centring, underlining etc., commanded by the operator) and a longitudinal parity check character for the block. Each character also has a parity bit. In the case of underlining the operator specifies the words to be underlined by actuating an underline key instead of the space key just before and after the (sequence of) word(s) to be underlined. Each of the data tracks also contains a table block containing a pair of bits for each data block in the track to indicate whether it is free and recordable, occupied and recordable, free but not recordable, or not usable. The table block also contains an instruction used to select the track having the first free and recordable block, the address of the first free and recordable block, and the identity of the cartridge. The remaining track contains the addresses of the blocks in the data tracks, and also contains programme blocks. The typewriter can be used to enter a text, this being passed via the core store to the tape loop where it is recorded in a sequence of free and recordable data blocks, the first of which was specified by a table block and the remainder of which were deduced from the bit-pairs in the table block (see above), the ether information in each data block (including the address of the next block in the sequence) being derived by the central unit and recorded also. The addresses of the blocks used are printed out at the line beginnings on the typewriter. The data entered is also printed. The operator can then order insertions and deletions of lines or paragraphs, alterations of line lengths and corrections of typing errors, lines being identified to the system by the block addresses typed out by the system. Insertions and deletions are performed by the system by altering the addresses in the data blocks which specify the respective next data blocks used for the text. The modified text can be printed out on the typewriter, with performance of the underlining etc. functions commanded. Centring is performed by adding space characters before and after the stored line, with incrementing of the stored indication of the number of characters in the line, until the latter equals the stored indication of the number of characters that the line can contain. Changes to information recorded on the tape are made by reading from tape to the core memory, making the changes, and writing back on to the tape. Justification can also be ordered, being performed by expanding interword spaces with incrementing of the indication in the block of the actual number of characters in the line until it equals the indication of the number that the line can contain.(From GB1410353 A)

abstract: The present invention relates to software and hardware technology. abstract: Methods, systems, and computer program products for auditing transactions involving sales of tickets by one business entity for a travel product provided by another business entity. title: Automatic quantitative barreling control system and method
abstract: The invention belongs to the technical field of chemical product liquid barreling, and particularly relates to an automatic quantitative barreling control system. The automatic quantitative barreling control system comprises an automatic quantitative control system and two barreling systems. Each barreling system is provided with one batch controller. Usually, a DCS of a control room conducts unified control and management according to issued delivery orders of an ERP management system, and when the DCS breaks down, the field batch controllers can be used for conducting local control, accordingly, the fault is scattered, and it is guaranteed that when the single fault point occurs, not all the barreling systems cannot be used. The batch controllers can control valve bodies of pneumatic cut-off valves with any aperture according to signal feedback of mass flow meters, and accordingly, flow can be controlled according to precision required by clients; when barreling is started, all the valve bodies are opened at a time or several times, and when the flow is close to the set value, the valve bodies are gradually closed till the small flow state is reached; and when the set value is reached, all the valve bodies are rapidly closed, and accurate barreling is achieved finally.

title: Autonomous convoy defense and comprehensive reconnaissance system
abstract: The present invention relates to an artificial intelligence-assisted autonomous convoy protection and reconnaissance system to enhance security and situational awareness in hostile or uncertain environments. The system comprises a plurality of unmanned aerial vehicles and a central command and control unit operating in a coordinated manner. A first set of aerial units function as a primary surveillance layer, performing continuous area scanning using multi-spectral sensors and onboard artificial intelligence for anomaly detection. Detected data is transmitted to the central control unit, which evaluates potential threats and supervises system operations. Upon identification of a suspected threat, secondary aerial units are selectively deployed to perform close-range reconnaissance, verification, and threat classification, thereby generating a structured threat profile. The system dynamically adapts its operational behaviour in response to risk levels, including perimeter monitoring and coordinated guidance support. Human-in-the-loop supervision is maintained at the command unit to authorize responses.

The safety verification method comprises the steps that S10, an industrial personal computer installs a certificate; step S20, applying for a Bin file from a server and analyzing the Bin file to obtain M1, M2, M3, U1, U2 and U3; step S30, acquiring a sequence code of the battery module, and awakening bms of the battery module; s40, communicating with the bs to obtain the ID of the electronic control unit; step S50, sending M1, M2, M3, U1, U2 and U3 to the battery module, and receiving M4, M5, U4 and U5 calculated by the battery module; step S60, the ID, M4, M5, U4 and U5 of the electronic control unit are encrypted, and ecuid, mkm4, mkm5, ukm4 and ukm5 are obtained; step S70, generating a verification XML file and an unlocking XML file based on the sequence code, the ecuid, the mkm4, the mkm5, the ukm4 and the ukm5; and step S80, verifying the battery module based on the verification XML file and the unlocking XML file. The method has the advantages that the verification safety of the battery module is greatly improved, and the nondestructive repair of the battery module is supported.

title: Battery test system
abstract: The present invention relates to a battery inspection system, and more particularly, to a battery inspection system capable of selectively operating a firefighting operation process based on a safety grade in a corresponding inspection room diagnosed by inspecting the performance and stability of a battery for each inspection room. To this end, the battery inspection system comprises: a plurality of inspection facilities individually arranged in each inspection room for inspecting a battery for an electric vehicle, and measuring battery information through safety and performance inspections; and an integrated management device arranged to be spaced from each inspection room through a partition wall, and classifying each battery information received from each inspection facility according to a room identification number. The integrated management device individually diagnoses a safety grade for each inspection room as any one among a normal step, an alarm step, and a suppression step based on a comparison deviation ratio between each performance information detected from the battery information for each inspection room and a reference value.COPYRIGHT KIPO 2025

title: Biometric garment and method of operation
abstract: A garment comprises a signal-activated fastener, embedded in the garment, which may be utilized to fastened/unfastened the garment upon receiving a signal. abstract: Systems, methods, and computer media implementing blockchain-based identity and transaction platforms are described herein.
