title: Bluetooth pairing system, method, and apparatus
abstract: Two Bluetooth enabled devices may communicate over a secure link provided they share the same link key which is used to mutual authentication and generation of encryption keys. A method for generating a link key is described which includes storing a partial link key in the device. A link key may then be generated when the associated secret key is provided to the device. This approach may be used in a bonding method in which a first device stores a link key, and a second device stores the associated partial link key. A system for providing link keys to a plurality of devices includes storing link keys in a first set of devices. The first set may be divided into several groups based on the stored link keys being associated with the same partial link key. A second set of devices store the set of all partial link keys and their associated group identifier. Bonding is performed by providing the group identifier and secret key associated with a device from the first set to a device in the second set. A secure system for remotely monitoring the status of a device using bonded Bluetooth devices is also described.

title: Charging pile data self-optimizing diagnosis system integrating clustering and deep learning
abstract: The invention discloses a self-optimizing diagnosis system for charging pile data by fusing clustering and deep learning. The acquisition module adopts an MEMS accelerometer, a microphone array, a thermal gradient sensor and a fluxgate sensor to acquire vibration, sound, heat and magnetism multi-mode signals in an event-driven and continuous sampling mode. The preprocessing module performs data quality evaluation and adaptive correction based on the unsupervised variation self-encoder. The feature fusion module extracts short-time Fourier transform and continuous wavelet transform features in parallel and dynamically distributes channel weights through a multi-head self-attention mechanism. The diagnosis engine adopts a lightweight depth network and combines structured pruning and incremental online learning to realize model hot update. The cloud knowledge base supports knowledge sharing across the charging pile group through induction transfer learning. The invention realizes the self-adaption and self-evolution diagnosis of the fault of the charging pile, and improves the diagnosis accuracy and the operation and maintenance efficiency.

Any one of the starting codes can be selected to be pasted when the starting codes are pasted, so that the construction efficiency of the charging station is improved, and the possibility of wrong pasting of the starting codes is avoided.

abstract: The invention provides a charging scheduling method and system for an electric vehicle charging station. abstract: The invention provides a charging station routing system, which is applied to at least one charging station located in a closed charging network. The charging station provides status information, and the status information optionally includes reading the user's identity information. The charging station routing system includes a cable, a connection port, a controller and a storage. One end of the cable can be connected to the charging station. The connection port is connected to the other end of the cable. The controller connection the connection port. The controller executes a charging station management application program and selects one from a communication protocol or a plurality of communication protocols, and can further establish a connection with the charging station through the connection port and the cable. The storage is connected to the controller to be able to record the status information. Wherein, after the controller establishes the connection with the charging station, at least a part of the control authority of the charging station is transferred to the controller, so that the charging station is managed by the controller.

title: Circuit arrangement for a telephone system, in particular a telephone private branch exchange, with the transfer of incoming calls to exchange plates and other telephone plates
abstract: 1334611 Automatic exchange systems SIEMENS AG 19 Nov 1971 [20 Nov 1970] 53758/71 Heading H4K In a PBX in which it is required to transfer an incoming call from one exchange operator to another, the first operator seizes a common call transfer device which is effective to set up a connection over the main speech switching network between the second operator's appearance thereon and the exchange line so that the two operators may converse via the network rather than via a special line. If the transfer is accepted the original operator releases her original connection to the exchange line via an auxiliary operator connector network and the call transfer device then makes a connection to the new operator via the auxiliary network and releases the path through the main network. The PBX normally permits direct inward dialling but access to operators occurs in the event of called extension busy or fails to answer, dilatory dialling on the part of the caller, or if an operator's position is specifically dialled. A calling exchange line AL is connected via its relay set A-Ue and a connector VK to a free register VS. A common control G-St then causes, if necessary, a connection to be set-up between VS and an operator VP via connector AK and a free supervisory set AS1. At the same time a free call transfer device PU is connected via connector PK to the set AS1 and the operator. The latter on ascertaining the caller's requirements may actuate a particular transfer key thus causing PU to seize the switching network marker M for the purpose of establishing a path between the register VS and the subscriber appearance TA which corresponds to the second operator, e.g. VPZ1, identified by operation of the transfer key. The identity of VPZ1 is stored in the transfer device. A lamp at the second operator's position is illuminated. When she is free she converses via her appearance TA with the first operator. (A split is effected in register VS to prevent the caller from overhearing the conversation.) If she accepts the call, VP withdraws thereby, via AS1, causing PU to seize common control G-St. The latter identifies AS 1 with the assistance of supervisory set hunter A-Su and causes the identity of the second operator, which is still stored in PU, to be passed via AS1 and AK into register VS where it replaces the first operator's identity in store NS. (Storage relay VZ denotes that the register is involved in an operator assistance call and not a direct inward dialling call.) VS advises G-St that the new identity is stored so that the existing connection via AS 1 may be broken down. Once this is effected, G-St is reseized to set up a new connection via ASZ 1 and to release the network path to TA.(From GB1334611 A)

title: Circuit arrangement for introducing a substitute clock signal into a pcm transmission system
abstract: At a main terminal connected to a remote terminal by way of a PCM signal path, a master clock controls the multiplexing of incoming messages from local lines for transmission over an outgoing line of that path to the remote terminal in a bipolar code enabling extraction of the clock frequency at the remote terminal. A discriminator at the main terminal continuously checks the operation of the master clock and, if that operation is normal, causes the transmission of a verification bit over the outgoing line to the remote terminal in an assigned time slot of a service channel of a period message frame; at the remote terminal, a detector responds to either the absence of the verification bit or the nonarrival of message signals to activate a standby clock controlling the sending of composite messages to the main terminal over an incoming line of the signal path. An extractor at the main terminal, connected to that incoming line, delivers the reconstituted pulses of the standby clock to the multiplexer in lieu of the output of the master clock if the latter operates improperly or not at all, as determined by the associated discriminator; a similar discriminator at the remote terminal may insert a corresponding verification bit into a service slot of a message frame transmitted to the main terminal to establish the correct functioning of the standby clock.(From [publication reference] A)

title: Circuit arrangement for telephone private branch exchanges with co-ordinate selectors
abstract: 940,091. Automatic exchange systems. TELEFONAKTIEBOLAGET L. M. ERICSSON. Jan. 8, 1960 [Jan. 12, 1959], No. 777/60. Heading H4K. In a PABX in which a link circuit such as SNR1 is connected to the called line over crossbar switches GVB1, SLVB1, a single wire serves for testing and for holding of the connection, and provision is made in certain circumstances for camping on a busy line and for breaking in. When connection is made to the wanted line, relay T5 is operated in the marker MT and relay S4 in the link SNR1, so that the c wire is connected to differential test relay T2. If the line is idle, the c wire is connected to resistance earth and T2 is inoperative. The marker is released and ringing takes place. The bridges of switches GVB1, SLVB1 are held from break contacts of S5 and G. If the line is busy, the c wire is earthed directly over the multiple and T2 energizes. Relay S5 pulls up and releases switch GVB1, while common relay R energizes and inserts rectifier L in the c wire so that SLVB1 is not held from the busy line. A preferred subscriber may break in by dialling a particular number, whereupon the marker is reconnected and relay T4 therein is energized from the register. Now, when T2 responds to the busy test, S5, R do not energize and the switches are therefore held. Relay S1 operates, holding the c wire when the marker releases, and extends a talking connection to the busy subscriber who is asked to hang up, whereupon S1 falls back and ringing occurs. Incoming calls are set up by an operator, each exchange line terminating in a link, Fig. 4 (not shown), somewhat similar to SNR1. An additional relay (F2) controlled by the operator enables her to make a talking connection to the wanted line. An exchange call can camp on a busy line and is automatically extended thereto when it becomes idle. Relay T1 in the marker MT allows the operator to receive a signal when a camping condition exists on a wanted busy line.(From GB940091 A)

title: Clamping device for a rim to be inspected in a testing machine
abstract: The clamping ring for vehicle wheel testing machines is constructed in two parts. The ring is in two halves (3, 4) each having welded flanges (7, 10) by which they may be coupled together and tightened around the rim of the wheel under test. Each half-ring has external radial arms (13, 14) formed from angled plates. Stacked laminations of magnetic material (16) are clamped between the plates to form a magnetic armature for each hafl-ring. The armatures are suspended over their respective electro-magnet coils so that when these are excited, the clamping ring transmits the oscillations to the wheel to produce flexural moments as required by the test procedure. The ring has elastic properties so that the loading on the rim is rotationally symmetrical.

title: Commerce-enabled environment for interacting with simulated phenomena
abstract: Methods and systems for interacting with simulated phenomena are provided. Example embodiments provide a Simulated Phenomena Interaction System "SPIS," which enables a user to incorporate simulated phenomena into the user's real world environment by interacting with the simulated phenomena. In one embodiment, the SPIS comprises a mobile environment (e.g., a mobile device) and a simulation engine. The mobile environment may be configured as a thin client that remotely communicates with the simulation engine, or it may be configured as a fat client that incorporates one or more of the components of the simulation engine into the mobile device. These components cooperate to define the characteristics and behavior of the simulated phenomena and interact with users via mobile devices. The characteristics and behavior of the simulated phenomena are based in part upon values sensed from the real world, thus achieving a more integrated correspondence between the real world and the simulated world. Interactions, such as detection, measurement, communication, and manipulation, typically are initiated by the mobile device and responded to by the simulation engine based upon characteristics and behavior of the computer-generated and maintained simulated phenomena.

abstract: The invention relates to the technical field of ocean engineering, in particular to a complex environment adaptive ship sand blasting robot cluster platform and a process thereof. title: Computer-aided system and method for the creation, verification, governance and execution of individual and corporate gift and benefit decisions in an AI-supported, policy or preference-compatible, security-controlled, trust-scoring, auditable and processable format.
abstract: Invention is a computer-aided system (100) and method for the creation, verification, governance and execution of individual and corporate gift and benefit decisions in an AI-supported, policy or preference-compatible, security-controlled, trust-scoring, auditable and operable manner. The system generates gift suggestions based on buyer context, sender intention, policy and budget rules, and product, seller, stock and delivery data and evaluates them with compliance, risk, trust and policy compliance scores (190). An embedded (510) or external (520) verifiable security-governance subsystem (200) calculates an execution confidence score with input/source/model output verification, policy/authority control, security risk analysis, and agent/vehicle call governance; it routes a rigid decision gate (470) proposal to a decision of permission, review, alternative, restricted execution, blocking, or undo, and stops it with an execution lock (479/480) when necessary. Each decision is stored as an object of proof (478) and an audit record (250). The system includes a universal catalog (280) with multi-source source-disclosure, a cross-site discovery and payment/gift trade orchestration layer (291); an agent-invocation/MCP agent (660) that calls only subsystem (200) vehicles and door-winding vehicles (661) that pass through the door (470); payment security analysis (780) of agent-initiated payments; an agent/payment security layer with agent-closed tokens (770) and execution locks (479); an agent/payment security layer that passes through each independent door life cycle (320) includes a privacy-protected preference vault (330) that does not open the recipient's sensitive preferences to the sender; a gift eligibility score (340) and fraud/abuse prevention (350); multilateral consent (370); and a gift transaction proof capsule (360) that connects the sender, recipient, decision, payment, code, delivery, donation, and return/dispute records with a hash chain. An execution takes place only when the valid proof capsule, permission decision, and idempotent key are provided together (default-rejection); scoring and decision are defined by a Trust-Door-Evidence (TGP) mathematical model.

title: Computer-integrated multi-gun welding system
abstract: A computer (20) executes a routine that allows supervision of a multi-gun welding system (26, 28), a programmable logic controller (22) controls movement of the guns and gun delivery devices, gun sensors measure the displacement of gun electrodes (29), delivery device sensors (33, 35) determine a location of the gun delivery devices, fixture sensors (41) measure the location of a workpiece fixture (40), a weld controller (34) applies power to the gun electrodes and an analog-to-digital converter converts the outputs of the sensors to digital signals readable by the computer. An embodiment of the weld routine executed by the computer spatially gauges the pre-weld fit-up of the workpieces and inhibits application of weld power if the fit-up is not within a specified tolerance, detects struck gun conditions after the weld, and diagnoses various faults during the welding based upon electrode position. A retro-fit gun sensor (30, 32) is disclosed which utilizes an electrode positioning bracket coupled to the electrode.

title: Control method and control device of locking device, equipment and storage medium
abstract: The invention discloses a control method and device of a locking device, equipment and a storage medium, and belongs to the technical field of vehicle-mounted equipment. The control method of the locking device comprises the following steps: when the locking device is in a locking state, in response to a received unlocking instruction, determining a risk level of the unlocking instruction according to an unlocking feature; under the condition that the risk level is lower than a first risk level threshold value, performing identity verification on an initiating main body of the unlocking instruction according to a verification condition; if the initiating main body of the unlocking instruction passes the identity verification, the locking device is controlled to execute an unlocking operation; if the initiating main body of the unlocking instruction does not pass the identity verification, the locking device is controlled to execute a first exception defense measure, and the first exception defense measure is used for blocking the unlocking instruction. By monitoring the risk level of the unlocking instruction and performing identity verification based on the risk level, the application can effectively intercept attacks of illegal unlocking instructions, and improve the intelligent protection level of the locking device.

title: Control method and device for electronic lock of charging pile and electronic equipment
abstract: The invention discloses a control method and device for an electronic lock of a charging pile and electronic equipment, and relates to the automobile charging technology. According to the method, after charging is started, whether the electric vehicle has a specific control function or not is determined according to a specific message sent by the electric vehicle. And under the condition that the electric vehicle does not have the specific control function, the electronic lock is controlled to be unlocked according to a preset unlocking rule of the charging pile. Under the condition that the electric vehicle has the specific control function, an unlocking instruction sent by the electric vehicle is detected; according to the control method, charging is stopped and the electronic lock is controlled to be unlocked under the condition that the unlocking instruction is detected, unlocking of the electronic lock according to the vehicle end equipment is achieved under the condition that the electric vehicle has a specific control function, unlocking of the electronic lock by the pile end equipment is achieved under the condition that the electric vehicle does not have the specific control function, and the control method is easy and convenient to operate and high in practicability. The operation steps of unlocking by a user can be greatly reduced, and the experience feeling of the user and the charging safety are improved.

title: Control method of standby spray gun in denitration system
abstract: The invention relates to the technical field of gas turbines, in particular to a control method for a standby spray gun in a denitration system. The method includes: acquiring all spray gun parameters, and setting a spray gun selection sequence according to all spray gun parameters; real-time flue gas parameters of the transition flue are obtained, and working parameters of the spray guns are set according to the real-time flue gas parameters and the spray gun selection sequence; and real-time operation state parameters of all the spray guns are obtained, and a correction instruction is generated according to the real-time operation state parameters. All the spray guns are recycled by setting the spray gun selection sequence and the working duration of the single spray gun, long-time operation of the single spray gun is avoided, and the use loss of the spray guns is reduced. And when the spray guns are abnormally tripped, the spray guns are started and stopped in sequence. And the spray gun which is abnormally tripped is fed with flushing water according to a sequential control quitting sequence, so that the spray gun is prevented from being overheated and crystallized to be blocked. The equipment safety of the tripped spray gun is guaranteed, meanwhile, the amount of urea sprayed into a hearth is also guaranteed, and NOx over-emission caused by the abnormal state of the spray gun can be effectively prevented.

abstract: The invention discloses a control method, a charging pile and electronic equipment. title: Control system for glass bending platen
abstract: A closed-loop control system for a hydraulically driven platen 74 for pressing a pane of glass. Through servo solenoid valve 112, the supply of fluid to cylinder 100, which actuates platen 74, is controlled. Linear motion transducer 120 is coupled to platen 74 and sends appropriate signals to programmable motion controller 134. The motion controller 134 controls a position module 140 functionally connected to the servo solenoid valve 112. The servo solenoid valve regulates the flow rate of fluid from the pump 104 to the cylinder 100. Motion controller 134 utilizes data from linear motion transducer 120 to make the modifications necessary to correctly execute the bending cycle of platen 74 based on a predetermined program. In the second embodiment of the present invention, a closed-loop control system for the hydraulically actuated platen 74 is utilized for precise control of the variable-speed pane glass conveyor means to improve the process of positioning the sheet glass S bent by the platen member 74.

In a computer system, a notification signal from a data processor specifying only that a data transfer with a particular data handling means is required is supplied to priority logic in an input/output controller, the priority logic obtaining a control item relating to the data handling means to be involved in a data transfer from a control item store holding a plurality of such items relating to respective data handling means and storing it in the input/output controller, the control item controlling data transfer between the data handling means and a memory and being modified and restored in the control item store. Processors communicate via respective main memories with peripheral sub-systems (each comprising one or more input/output or bulk memory devices) via a common input/output controller and priorityordered peripheral channels (one per peripheral sub-system). The input/output controller is under overall control of control words (" control items ") from one (only) of the main memories, the relevant memory being selected by a control panel. The controller has its own microprogramme store, and buffer store for data transfers. The control word specifies the operation required, the address of the peripheral subsystem, the address of the particular device within the latter (if there are more than one), and in the case of data transfer, the first address in main memory to supply or receive data and the amount of data to be transferred. The control word is read from its main memory, used, the main memory address field in it incremented, and then stored back in main memory. Data, command and status parallel characters (with parity bit) can be transferred to and from the peripheral sub-systems, preceded by read or write clock signals in both directions. Further status and other signal lines are provided. A data transfer operation may be terminated by the peripheral sub-system or the input/output controller, when the required number of characters has been transferred, or on detection of an error by the peripheral subsystem.(From GB1186414 A)

abstract: The application relates to the technical field of mobile charging vehicles, in particular to a cooperative control method for a discharging process. According to the method, a central coordination system is established through the whole vehicle controller, and an energy storage system, a charging system, a thermal management system and a driving system are integrated, so that full-flow automatic control of discharging is realized. The system comprises a state machine management module for maintaining five running states, a subsystem cooperation module for realizing the interlocking of a driving system through a heartbeat detection mechanism, a fault diagnosis module for monitoring voltage, current and temperature parameters in real time and executing protection actions, and a power regulation module for dynamically regulating discharge power by adopting a piecewise linear strategy according to the residual electric quantity of a battery. The application realizes the automatic coordination of the discharging process, improves the operation efficiency by more than thirty percent, eliminates the safety risk through an interlocking mechanism, greatly improves the usability of the system, and prolongs the cycle service life of the battery to more than one and two times of the original level.

title: Cryptographically Secure, Multilayered Authentication and Real-Time Traceable Product Authenticity Verification System and Method
abstract: This invention is about a computer-based system and method that enables integrated verification of product originality, display of product information to the consumer, and provide statistical reporting labeled location and date to the manufacturer using the cryptographic QR code specific to each product unit. In the system, a composite verification code consisting of three separate segments: vendor identification segment, product identification segment and unit uniqueness segment is produced by using cryptographically secure number generator for each product unit. This composite code is encrypted and embedded in the QR code using a symmetric encryption algorithm AES-256-GCM with a unique initialization vector in each encryption transaction. Upon scanning the QR code by the consumer, a three-layer verification door applies the steps of bot detection with user agent analysis, human verification with CAPTCHA mechanism and consumer authentication, respectively. During the AES-256-GCM decryption process, it is automatically determined whether encrypted data is manipulated via authentication label verification. Comprehensive metadata including IP address, geographical location, device type, consumer ID is collected in each scanning event, and suspicious activities are detected in real time with a multivariable algorithm. This invention is distinguished from the existing technique in terms of combining security with traceability (vendor + product + unit), integrating consumer authentication into the verification process and ensuring physical access control with the recording of each scan in an identified, positioned and behavioral analysis and placement of the QR label in the packaging, providing the consumer with product information (production location, manufacturer, party number, production date, SKT) and transparency of scan number and reporting each scan to the manufacturer with location and date label. By physically preserving the encrypted QR code at a location where the consumer product can be seen when consumed, only the person consuming the product can scan the code. Thanks to this system, all kinds of medical supplies, medicines and food products that are low-priced but important for human and public health can be protected against authenticity at very low costs.

title: Cyber-invader quantum security computer system
abstract: The invention presents a quantum security blockchain communication framework, a computer system and connected methods that protect civilian or military systems against quantum attacks, the Quantum Cyberattack Control Module, a rotary identity update and validation framework, methods for producing zero proof of trust, and a quantum blockchain system. The proposed discovery allows communication and functional requirements between systems to be secure against quantum attacks. This discovery allows the ability of compute units with limited data processing capabilities to acquire the ability to transmit classified data protected against quantum attacks through a rotary authentication and authentication mechanism. Periodically update the system's security keys to establish a reconciliation between the edge nodes is essentially the system's property; command-control communication, event-organization management, change-of-authority, authentication and herd missions make their functions secure in the quantum age. The proposed cyber invasion prosecutor quantum security computer provides a leading approach to security upgrades of existing systems without requiring physical quantum networks because it provides data security at a quantum level in environments with limited processing power without centralization. The cyber invasion prosecutor quantum security computer, protected by a zero-information and zero-confidence approach to which switches are routinely updated, reduces the memory need and cost to calculate on the blockchain, improving speed of communication and system security. By analyzing the danger in cross-cyber threat environments, the system chooses the most suitable privacy method for attacks, preventing the functional flow of the system from being compromised. The current invention efficiently attains quantum-level security without the need for additional costs.

abstract: Data is transmitted or received by a master processing unit (12) through a data channel (16) which is coupled to a slave processing unit (not shown). Information bits are transmitted by the master unit (12) only in conjunction with such clock pulses, and information bits are received by the slave processing unit only upon receipt of clock pulses transmitted through the data channel (16). Transmission by the slave unit and reception by the master unit (12) through data channel (16) are similarly controlled by the clock pulses. Short data pulses signify binary zeros, and longer data pulses signify binary ones.

title: Data modem with connection test and automatic disconnection device
abstract: Modems including line verification circuits for automatically advising that a direct distance dialed network has been connected between the communicating modems with echo suppressors in the network disabled, is disclosed. The line verification circuitry is either identical for all modems or may be master/slave equipment. The line verification circuitry includes a first tone generator for emitting a unique tone for disabling echo suppressors in the telephone line. A tone generator at a communicating modem, upon receiving the unique tone, emits a different tone which is not capable of disabling the echo suppressors but is capable of transmission through the telephone line when the echo suppressors are disabled. In one preferred embodiment, the second tone is near the limit of the telephone line bandwidth, and thus its reception is an indication that an acceptable line for data has been established between the modems. Circuitry at both modems is responsive to the first and second tones for automatically verifying the existence of the desired communication link. Upon completion of data transmission, the modem itself will automatically disconnect the existing telephone line if the data terminal equipment associated with the modems does not have such capability.(From [publication reference] A)

title: Deterministic fleet continual learning and adaptive validation architecture for distributed autonomous systems
abstract: A distributed autonomous system architecture enforces deterministic, version-pinned policy execution through operating system memory protection mechanisms while enabling continuous policy improvement via centralized constrained reinforcement learning. title: Device and method for simulating hazardous material detection
abstract: The present invention is a device that simulates both a radioactive and/or hazardous chemical source and a radioactivity and/or hazardous chemical detector, to train individuals in the correct use of a real radioactivity and/or hazardous chemical detector. A passive radio identification device (PRID) is used to simulate the hazardous material source. The PRID includes a tuned circuit, an energy storage capacitor, a transmitter unit, a microcomputer and a magnet. The simulated detector includes a hall effect device to detect the magnet. When the magnet is detected, (when a trainee moves the simulated detector close to the PRID), the simulated detector outputs a 50ms RF burst. The RF pulse resonates the tuned circuit contained within the PRID, and a voltage is developed across the tuned circuit. This voltage charges the energy storage capacitor through a diode. When the capacitor is charged, the microcomputer is activated by the power supplied by the storage capacitor. Once activated, the microcomputer waits for completion of the 50ms pulse, and then activates the transmitter. The transmitter then transmits a signal that identifies the type of contamination to the simulated detector. The transmitter uses the tuned circuit as an antenna.

title: Dispatch-based responder camera activation
abstract: A method of automatic activation of a responder camera to begin capturing a video can be performed by a computing device. The computing device receives an indication of a location or an event. The computing device determines a geographic area associated with the location or event. The computing device receives a dispatch acknowledgement from a responder, where the dispatch acknowledgement indicates that the responder is at the geographic area or that the responder is en route to the geographic area. The responder camera is configured to begin capturing a video in response to receiving the camera activation signal.

The ball path selector unit comprises a plurality of groups of relay-operated, normally open contacts, each group of contacts corresponding to a particular pin position, and the contacts thereof being closed when the pin sensing mechanism detects that the corresponding pin is standing on the playing deck. Depending on the combination of pins remaining standing after the first ball of the frame, the associated circuit of contacts in the ball path selector unit is made, and the indicator operated to illustrate the optimum ball path for that particular pin combination. The lamps or switches referred to above respectively illuminate arrows on an indicator board (Fig. 11), or control the travel of an index number 152 round the periphery of the indicator board (Fig. 8) so that the index is arrested at the optimum point of entry of the ball into the array. The indicators illustrated additionally comprise an array of lamps corresponding with an array of ten pins on the playing deck of the alley, the lamps being selectively operated by the pinsensing means to give a visual indication on the indicator of the pins remaining standing after the first ball of the frame. The apparatus may also comprise switches for operation by the bowler and which control means on the indicator for indicating the optimum ball path for the first ball of the frame.(From GB1030191 A)

title: Distributed file and record locking
abstract: An improvement is disclosed to the conventional single node operating system to provide a distributed file management system (DFS) with a plurality of nodes (A,B) and a plurality of files (5). The DFS uses the UNIX operating system tree structure employing inodes (data structure containing administrative information for each file (151,152) to manage the local files and surrogate inodes (s_inode) to manage access to files existing on another node. In addition, the DFS uses a lock table to manage the lock status of files. The method which implements the DFS locking of records and files involves the following steps. If the file is a local file, then the UNIX operating system standard file is used. However, if a remote file is to be locked, the UNIX operating system LOCLF and FCNTL system calls are intercepted and a remote process call (RPC) DFS_LOCK_CONTROL is executed. The server node (A) receives the remote process call and carries out the lock request. The request could entail locking a single record, a set records or the whole file. The server then acknowledges receipt of the RPC by sending a signal while the client surrogate inode is waiting for a reply from the DFS_LOCK_CONTROL RPC. The client confirms the reception of the lock and sends an acknowledgement to the remote server. The server updates the lock table after receiving the ackowledgement, then DFS_LOCK_CONTROL'S acknowledgement, then DFS_LOCK_CONTROL updates the lock table.(From [publication reference] A2)

title: Electronic data processing system
abstract: 1284298 Data transmission HONEYWELL Inc 17 Sept 1969 [28 Oct 1968] 45849/69 Heading G4A Digital data transfer between a memory 16 and peripheral units 19 in separate sectors 1-3 is regulated by dividing the time available in at least one sector into time slots and selectively allocating the time slots to the peripheral units collectively and/or individually in relation to their data transfer rates. This patent has features in common with Specification 1,107,661. The apparatus.-A multiprogrammed system comprises a word organized processor 10, a character organized processor 12 operating in a variable length mode, an 1/0 controller 14, and a plurality of memory modules in memory 16 having some protected areas, all controlled by a master programme for parallel data transfer. Processor 10 has a multiprogramming capability and includes sequence counters, index registers, interrupt registers and masking registers. The 1/0 controller 14 (Fig. 2, not shown) sends data between memory 16 and peripheral units 19 in response to request from processors 10, 12. Upon receiving such a request, the controller 14 assigns a read/write circuit therein to interconnect the requested peripheral unit with memory 16. Each circuit includes a storage register identifying the currently addressed memory location and the other stores a starting address where the data to be transfered is stored. The peripheral units are divided into sectors 1-3, each sector having different peripheral control units CUl-CUN. Each sector has a memory slot assignment table in the 1/0 controller 14 which stores control information relating to the processing of instructions involving peripheral devices in the sector. It functions as a memory cycle distributer whose cycling period defines a number of time slot intervals, e.g. six in Fig. 2 and 3 (not shown), each having two control words. Also provided is time slot activity storage with six elements for each sector and means for checking the availability of time slots in a sector, updating and clearing time slot data. Operation.-The assignment of time slot intervals to a peripheral unit involves determining the availability of a read/write circuit, searching the time slot activity table to see if sufficient time slot intervals are available in that sector to accommodate the data transfer rate of the peripheral unit, and assigning the time slot intervals.(From GB1284298 A)

title: Elements for manufacturing pneumatic logic systems with integrated circuits
abstract: 1413174 Valves LA TELEMECANIQUE ELECTRIQUE 29 Sept 1972 [29 Sept 1971] 45206/72 Heading F2V [Also in Divisions F1 and G4] A fluid switching circuit comprises a number of modules. Each module has, on opposite faces, inlet and exit ports which communicate with the corresponding ports of the adjacent modules and comprises an AND gate and a bistable unit. The gate and bi-stable may be separable sub-modules. Fluid-tight communication between the ports is established by face to face contact and 0-rings. The circuit described is a pneumatic programmer in which, at each step in a cycle, one stage of the circuit provides an output signal S to a machine. When the machine has performed the operation so ordered, the circuit receives a signal R which energizes the next stage, resetting the presently energized stage. In the embodiment shown in Fig. 3 each module comprises submodules 1 and 2. Each AND gate forms part of sub-module 2 which can be mounted on tie rods 4, the inlet and outlet ports communicating when adjacent modules abut. The bottom face of the module has connectors for securing flexible tubes carrying signals to and from the machine. The top face has inlet and outlet ports which communicate with ports in the base of submodule 1, which contains the bi-stable. The sub-module 1 has resilient catches 6 to snapengage in grooves 7 of the sub-module 2. The sub-module 1, Fig. 4, comprises a bistable element in which the presence of a fluid input signal X1 from the AND gate or of a manual input X1 by way of push-button 13 causes fluid P from a power source to pass to an outlet x, the disc 32 being moved to the right. An input X0, which may also be fluid or manual, moves the disc leftwards where it is held by magnetic action and prevents fluid flow from P to x. A visual pressure indicator 11 is provided. The sub-module 2, Fig. 5, comprises AND gate 3 having a double headed free piston 14. Fluid appears at a central output only when fluid prosis applied to both inputs x and R. The circuit may be associated with logic units since, for example, when a particular step of the cycle is reached it may be necessary to cause the machine to perform a number of operations before proceeding to the next step. The logic unit ensures that a signal R stepping the programmer cannot be generated until all these operations have been completed. Similarly if a particular operation is to be performed at more than one step the outputs of the relevant stages must be connected to the machine via an OR circuit.(From GB1413174 A)

title: Endwise - a decentralized will and testament system
abstract: A decentralized system for wills and testaments can include a user interface and a backend consisting of single or multiple smart contracts deployed on any blockchain system (public or private) to ensure transparency and data integrity through the immutability of smart contracts. Personally identifiable information (PII), including but not limited to name and email, can be stored off-chain on a traditional centralized database or a decentralized database solution such as GunDB with encryption using various encryption algorithms such as AES-256 to ensure data privacy. Asset details, beneficiary details, and other information critical to the functioning of different modules of the proposed system can be stored off-chain on a permanent storage solution such as IPFS or Swarm, which can be encrypted using various encryption algorithms such as AES-256. The smart contract may contain a reference to the stored data along with a checksum, which can be a hash of the contents of the data or any other security measure to ensure data integrity. The reference will depend on the type of off-chain permanent storage solution used. In the case of IPFS, it can be a CID that can be accessed via the IPFS protocol or using a public IPFS gateway. The key for decrypting the data stored on the off-chain permanent storage can be stored locally if necessary to ensure complete privacy. The user can also opt for a shared key approach wherein a part of the key is shared with other beneficiaries. The system may monitor for a triggering event, such as but not limited to uploading a verified death certificate or failure to respond to a periodic confirmation message. In such cases, the code in the smart contract will be automatically executed, and the beneficiaries added by the user will be notified. This proposed solution is privacy-focused, transparent, and emphasizes on decentralization and data integrity.

title: Enhanced real-time electromagnetic field detection and analysis system
abstract: An enhanced electromagnetic field detection and analysis system employs three orthogonal magnetic field sensors within a Faraday cage construction to detect and analyze electromagnetic field events. The system features high-speed data acquisition operating at 8 billion samples per second coupled with a circular buffer memory system storing 16,000 sample points, enabling detection of field strengths from 100 V/m to 100,000 V/m and frequencies between 10 MHz and 10 GHz. The system performs real-time Fast Fourier Transform analysis up to 7 GHz while maintaining detection capabilities at distances up to 100 meters. Housed in an anodized aluminum exterior with compartmentalized interior spaces, the system provides continuous monitoring, sophisticated frequency analysis, and threat assessment through building perimeter software, operating without sacrificial elements and maintaining performance in various environmental conditions. The system enables identification of specific electromagnetic signatures through advanced signal processing and maintains historical data for forensic analysis.

title: Fail safe architecture for a computer system
abstract: The fail safe architecture (26) for a computer system (10) includes a read only memory (ROM) self-check module (22), a random access memory (RAM) self-check module (24) and operation code instructions (op code) self-check module which are actuated periodically by a non-maskable interrupt (NMI) to a microprocessor (14). The microprocessor then suspends the current applications routine being executed. If the self-check module detects a failure, the microprocessor enters a fail safe trap routine which initially resynchronizes the operation of the microprocessor and then delays the generation of a critical timing pulse (fail safe trigger ) with a series of ''jump to yourself'' steps. The fail safe trigger signal activates a device (18) which sends a fail safe square wave to a narrow bandwith, digital, band-pass filter (400). If the fail safe square wave signal is not supplied to the filter during a prescribed period of time, a set of transistor switches (Q1, Q2), interposed between the computer system power supply (30) and the voltage regulator for the computer system, is not actuated and power is cut off to the computer system. Otherwise, if the fail safe signal is received within the prescribed window of time, switches are actuated to couple the power supply to the computer system.

title: Hardware-rooted execution-finality system for sovereign artificial intelligence infrastructure, ai-native telecommunications and satellites
abstract: A hardware-backed execution-ﬁnality architecture is disclosed for sovereign AI infrastructure, GPU fabrics, AI-native telecommunications, satellite networks, and CBDC settlement infrastructure. The architecture enforces a fail-closed model wherein a Candidate Act generated by a GPU cluster, artiﬁcial intelligence system, or digital wallet is held in a non-effective state prior to egress. Within a protected enforcement domain, the Candidate Act is canonicalized into a machine-veriﬁable descriptor, technical authority predicates are validated, and a tamper-evident validation receipt is committed atomically with capability release. Upon successful validation, a scoped, non-bearer capability is issued and subsequently veriﬁed by a hardware-rooted Finality Sink before external effectuation. By decoupling rigorous authority validation from high-speed veriﬁcation, the system enables line-rate cryptographic enforcement across GPU interconnects, data-processing units, satellite egress points, and CBDC ledgers. The architecture thereby technically gates the transition from computational intent to external consequence, ensuring computation alone does not impart authority.

title: Human rights in conflict zones: system for legal protections and global responsibility
abstract: The present invention relates to a comprehensive system for protecting human rights in conflict zones through an integrated legal and technological infrastructure. Armed conflicts frequently result in serious violations, including unlawful detention, torture, sexual violence, forced displacement, and deliberate attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure. Although international humanitarian law and international human rights law provide established standards for protection and accountability, enforcement mechanisms remain fragmented, delayed, and vulnerable to political and operational constraints. The invention addresses these shortcomings by creating a secure, interoperable platform that enables real-time documentation, verification, legal classification, and coordinated international response. The system comprises encrypted reporting interfaces accessible through mobile and web-based devices, allowing victims, witnesses, and authorized personnel to safely submit multimedia evidence. Each submission is authenticated באמצעות cryptographic hashing and preserved באמצעות a tamper-resistant distributed ledger to ensure integrity and chain-of-custody. An artificial intelligence-driven legal analysis engine processes incoming reports, categorizes alleged violations under applicable legal frameworks, and generates structured assessments suitable for judicial or investigative review. The invention further integrates satellite imagery and geospatial monitoring tools to corroborate reported incidents, enhancing evidentiary reliability and reducing misinformation. A built-in victim protection framework provides configurable anonymity controls, encrypted communications, and secure data compartmentalization to safeguard sensitive information. Additionally, automated alert mechanisms identify patterns of escalating or systematic abuses and notify relevant oversight bodies to facilitate timely intervention. By unifying digital evidence preservation, automated legal analysis, geospatial verification, and global coordination within a single system, the invention establishes a proactive and standardized approach to human rights protection in armed conflict. It strengthens accountability pathways, enhances transparency, and reinforces the principle that human rights protections remain enforceable even in the most volatile conflict environments.

In this way, the reliability of images in city centers can be verified in real time, image reliability is ensured over the existing 5G-Advanced/6G infrastructure without incurring additional costs, and reliable results are achieved even in adverse weather conditions. The invention protects the public from misleading content by providing the possibility to verify reliable video content without harming personal privacy.

title: Improved metering systems & methods
abstract: A flow meter run offers autonomous operation whilst improving measurement performance & confidence, increased safety and improving the total cost of ownership. A plurality of isolation valve assemblies each offer DBB (Double Block & Bleed) isolation to isolate a component or meter run section. This DBB isolation includes components being extracted from the main metering line. The meter run philosophy is detailed with use of a novel rotational orifice meter, though other flow meters may be substituted. The flow meter run also features extractable filters, a rotational and extractable flow conditioner which includes open and blind isolation components. The rotational orifice meter can house several independent orifice plates or nozzles and extractable sample probes and temperature elements. Further instrument sensors include the direct (non-inferred) measurement of density and/or viscosity. The system is configured for multiple sensors to monitor performance, autonomy, validation and isolation.

title: Improved method for controlling reducing atmosphere in rotary kiln
abstract: The invention relates to the technical field of cement manufacturing, and provides an improved method for controlling a reducing atmosphere in a rotary kiln. The sparks of the five-stage discharging pipe are checked through the first spark observation opening, so that the spark condition appearing in the first spark observation opening is eliminated; after it is confirmed that no spark exists in the fifth-stage discharging pipe through a first spark observation opening, the state of the spark at the tail of the kiln is checked through a throat of the smoke chamber at the tail of the kiln; detecting the content of Fe < 2 + > in the clinker discharged from the rotary kiln so as to determine the reducing atmosphere state in the rotary kiln; according to the determined state of the reducing atmosphere in the rotary kiln, outer axial flow air and/or inner rotational flow air are/is adjusted, so that the burn-off rate of pulverized coal is increased by reducing the length of a black fire head of flame, and the purpose of improving the reducing atmosphere in the rotary kiln is achieved. The invention provides an efficient reducing atmosphere detection mode, so that the reducing atmosphere control in the whole cement manufacturing process can be repeatedly operated, and the state can be accurately verified.

abstract: 763,830. Electric digital-data-storage apparatus. STANDARD TELEPHONES & CABLES, Ltd. April 26, 1954, No. 11970/54. Class 106 (1). Storage equipment for intelligence in electrical form comprises a number of stores each capable of storing a related set of signals by means of a temporary reversible change in condition of a storage medium, the set of signals including an identification signal or signal group and an information signal or signal group; recording means associated with said stores and adapted to store intelligence in said stores; reading means associated with said stores and adapted to scan intelligence stored in said stores; control equipment for registering any one of a number of identification signals or signal groups; a comparator for comparing an identification signal or signal group read from a store with an identification signal or signal group from said control equipment to determine whether there is a predetermined relation between them; and means for performing a further operation in respect of the information signal or signal group in a store whose identification signal or signal group has been found to have the said predetermined relation with the control identification signal or signal group. The apparatus described enables the total charge payable by each of 100 telephone subscribers to be computed from a register of all the calls made by the subscribers, the register being a track on a magnetic drum in each sector of which is recorded the details of one call. Each track section, Fig. 2, contains three groups of four digits for recording, in a binary-decimal scale, the subscriber's number and the call fee, and a spare digit position used for a reset pulse. To each of 100 gates is applied two inputs, one from a 100-stage counter chain and one from one of the 100 outputs of a staticisor-tree arrangement for the " identity " digits. The counter chain advances one stage at the end of each revolution of the drum and the staticisor-tree is cleared as the " reset " digit of each track section is read. During the first revolution of the drum, every time a track section relating to subscriber 1 is read the output from the tree passes through gate 1 (not shown) and is used to gate the following " fee " digits to a computer, and during revolution 2 every time a section relating to subscriber 2 is read the output from the tree passes through gate 2 (not shown) and is used to gate the following " fee " digits to the computer. This cycle is continued and after 100 revolutions it will be possible to obtain the total charge for each subscriber. Specification 763,828, [Group XXXIX], is referred to.

title: Improving aerodynamic stability with plasma based flow control in aircraft with single pivot oblique wing structures
abstract: This invention is related to plasma based active flow control system and method to reduce asymmetric flow separation, rolling moment and divergence moment imbalances due to arrow angle in aircraft with single pivot oblique wing structures. The system includes a segmented DBD plasma actuator array (20) that can be driven independently over an oblique wing structure (16) that can rotate around a single pivot point, a forward swept first wing half (18) and a backscavenged second wing half (19), an arrow angle / wing position detection unit (21), a plasma drive unit (20) that provides the segmented DBD plasma actuator array (23), a frequency, task cycle, phase difference, pulse mode and/or segment activation order, and a plasma drive unit (23) that determines the control segments (1 control segments) of each actuator according to the arrow angle, flow conditions and flow conditions and/or aerodynamic feedback data. The control unit (11) differentiates voltage, frequency, duty cycle, phase difference, pulse mode and/or segment activation sequence through the plasma drive unit (23), thus differentially reducing the effects of flow separation and moment imbalance occurring in the swept and swept wing halves. Thus, it is possible to reduce aerodynamic instabilities specific to single-pivot oblique wing geometry, improve flight stability and provide active flow control adaptable to variable flight conditions.

title: In situ waste impoundment treating apparatus and method of using same
abstract: An apparatus (U) is shown in figures 11-13 that includes a power operated vehicle (V) that supports a vertically movable frame (W) that has a confined space defining shround (X) on the lower end thereof that may be placed in sealing contact with the upper surface of a hazardous waste impoundment (Y) at a first station to permit the in situ detoxification of a desired portion of the impoundment. At least one power driven blade (Z) is rotated downwardly from within the shroud (X) into the impoundment to form a vertically extending zone (A-1) of particled material that is treated with a detoxifying agent that may be chemical, biological or heat from one or more plasma torches. title: Intelligent early warning charging pile arc detection method and system
abstract: The invention discloses an intelligent early warning charging pile arc detection method and system, and belongs to the technical field of charging pile electrical safety detection. The method comprises the following steps: performing multiplexing configuration on an arc detection function in a charging pile power control system to obtain full-link electrical state information, and according to adaptive frequency domain analysis, establishing a dynamic noise baseline by using a working condition noise mapping model driven by charging communication protocol state data to obtain spectrum residual data; and inputting the extracted multi-dimensional feature vectors into a lightweight machine learning classification model for arc event discrimination, verifying whether an arc exists or not through active power disturbance when a discrimination result is in a suspected interval, and executing a hierarchical protection response strategy according to confidence and a verification conclusion. And predictive maintenance early warning is realized through historical data longitudinal trend analysis across charging sessions. According to the method, fault arc detection coverage and risk trend pre-judgment of the charging full link are realized on the premise that special sensor hardware is not added.

Wire brushes 84 rotate and engage the top signatures of the stack to depress them and aid alignment. A detector switch 55 indexes the support bars 74 down as the stack forms until, at a certain stack height, a switch (65), Fig. 3 (not shown), causes the conveyers 10, 12 to slow down and conveyer 14 to stop, the support bars 74 being rapidly lowered to a conveyer 86, the belts 87 of which remove the stack. Conveyers 10, 12 are then stopped, the previously fed signatures being piled up by the blade 38 until the bars 74 return to their original position when the conveyers 10, 12, 14 are again driven at normal speed. title: Liquid shot blasting control method for blade
abstract: The invention aims to provide a liquid shot blasting control method for a blade. The method comprises the following steps of (1) determining the shot blasting saturation intensity and shot blasting parameters; (2) determining the diameter of a shot jet indentation; (3) determining the coordinates of the outer contour of the blade; (4) determining a blade body shot blasting path; (5) setting the rotating speed; (6) determining a blade fillet path; and (7) carrying out liquid shot blasting on the blade. The method reduces the damage risks of scratches, inlaying and the like of shots to the surface of a part, and the dispersion degree of blade surface residual stress is small. The variable coefficient of residual compressive stress data is 0.06 after shot blasting is carried out on the titanium alloy blade through the shot blasting method, and the variable coefficient of residual compressive stress data is 0.10 after shot blasting is carried out in a traditional shot blasting mode. After the method is implemented, the shot-blasted blade not only meets the blade surface quality requirement, but also has the smaller dispersion degree of surface residual stress, the fatigue life of the blade is better prolonged, and the reliability and durability of a gas turbine unit are improved finally.

title: Machine learning based system and method for terrorist group attribution and incident prediction using ensemble classification
abstract: The present invention discloses a machine learning-based system (100) and method for automated attribution of terrorist incidents to perpetrator groups. The system includes a data acquisition module (110) for receiving incident data with geospatial and temporal attributes, and a preprocessing engine (120) for filtering and feature transformation. An ensemble classification module (130) integrates XGBoost classifier (132) and LightGBM classifier (134) through a softvoting classifier (136). A temporal validation module (140) performs chronological train-test splits to evaluate generalization, and a feature importance analyzer (150) ranks predictive features. The system achieves 97.39 percent accuracy on standard validation and 95.02 percent on temporal validation. Feature analysis identifies latitude, longitude, and year as dominant predictors, indicating that geospatial-temporal patterns form the primary operational signature. The invention serves as a proof-of-concept tool for counterterrorism intelligence support.

abstract: The invention provides a manufacturing process for simulation glass used for a model car. abstract: The invention discloses a medicinal product storage cabinet. title: Memory arrangement for receiving and reproducing code characters, in particular for telewriting exchanges
abstract: 790,914. Telegraph exchange systems. STANDARD TELEPHONES & CABLES, Ltd. June 4, 1954 [June 10, 1953], No. 15939/53. Drawings to Specification. Class 40 (3). In a telegraph exchange system comprising a number of non-expendible message stores, such as tracks on a magnetic drum, with automatic switching equipment for distributing incoming messages from a number of incoming channels to empty stores available to all said channels and automatically allocated when required for use, together with supervisory storage equipment to record the identity of each incoming message and the empty store or stores to which it has been allocated and means for determining the order of retransmission of all stored messages, means are incorporated for retransmitting each of the stored messages in accordance with destination information carried by each message directly from the store or stores in which it was originally stored. In the arrangement described, storage members, additional to those used as the main or message stores, are included between the latter and the outgoing line, but these serve primarily as operational devices, and incidentally as temporary stores, for enabling a change in transmission speed to be effected between the rate at which the characters are detected and read off from the main storage member or members and passed to registers operating to pass on the telegraph signals at the normal teleprinter speed. Apart from these " speed-changing " devices, the retransmission of the message takes place directly from the member or members of the common store in which the incoming message has been recorded for subsequent disposal. The identification of the message in the common store may be determined by the number of the incoming line, the priority of the message and the number or numbers of the common storage tracks on which the message is to be found. The description, in so far as it relates to the reception of the message, storage on one or more of the tracks of the common store, the registration of the message on a booking track, and the operation of discriminating means to detect the completed message of highest priority in the common store and the presentation of the first line of the message on an operator's teleprinter, is substantially identical with that inincluded in Specifications 788,991 and 788,992. The further arrangements for disposing of the message and described in connection with Figs. 22 to 29 (not shown) relate to the association of an outgoing line track on the drum with a register for passing the characters to the selected outgoing line at teleprinter speed, and automatic means for connecting the line track to the track or tracks of the common store in accordance with the information on the booking track pertaining to the message selected for disposal by reason of its priority. The operation of keys by an operator initiates the booking operation, selects the line for which the message is intended and a combination of keys represents in binary form the priority of the message. When the next free section of the booking track is reached, the priority of the message is recorded followed by the binary equivalent of the tens and units numbers of the common storage track containing the message. If the outgoing line associated with the booking track is free the message priorities set up in the booking track are examined and when the highest priority has been found, this information is erased from the booking track and the booking information set up on a pattern register used in the priority comparison is utilized to connect the common storage track to the line track leading to the pattern movement register for transferring the telegraph characters to the outgoing line. This is effected by two ten-position switches which are stepped to positions corresponding to the number of the common storage track carrying the message and allow the outputs of the associated read head to pass to the record head co-operating with the outgoing line track. Specifications 713,902, [Group XL (c)], and 762,094 also are referred to.(From GB790914 A)

title: Method and apparatus for checking fire detectors
abstract: A fire detector checking method and device are disclosed for nondestructively verifying the operation of installed fire detectors of the type which operate on the principle of detecting the rate of temperature rise of the ambient air to sound an alarm and/or which sound an alarm when the temperature of the ambient air reaches a preset level. The fire alarm checker device of the instant invention uses the principle of effecting a controlled simulated alarm condition to ascertain whether or not the detector will respond. In the preferred embodiment, the checker comprises a hand-held instrument employing a controlled heat source, e.g., an electric lamp having a variable input, for heating at a controlled rate an enclosed mass of air in a first compartment, which air mass is then disposed about the fire detector to be checked. A second compartment of the device houses an electronic circuit to sense and adjust the temperature level and heating rate of the heat source. Actuation of a fire detector of the rate of rise type within a predetermined time interval after applying the heated air mass thereto verifies the soundness of the system. A technique is further disclosed whereby a test for proper operation at a predetermined temperature level may separately or alternatively be performed by the novel device on fire detectors which are triggered at some predetermined temperature level irrespective of the rate of temperature rise.

abstract: The method and the apparatus are used for securely controlling an elevator system (3) comprising a drive unit (38) which allows an elevator car (36) located in an elevator shaft (35) to move and which is controlled in a secured manner by a control device (100) in such a way that during normal operation, the elevator car (36) can move to at least two access points to the elevator shaft (35) at which doors (30A, 30B) are provided. The monitoring unit (10A; 10B) is connected to the monitoring sensor (11A; 11B) and, in the autonomous mode, monitors the state of the monitoring sensor (11A; 11B) and records state data; furthermore, the monitoring unit (10A; 10B) is connected to a securing unit (1) which reads the recorded state data from all connected monitoring units (10A; 10B), evaluates said state data and prevents the elevator system (3) from being put into the normal mode of operation if a change in the state of one of the monitored doors (30A; 30B) has been detected. The monitoring sensor (11A, 11B) is a switching contact which is coupled to the associated door lock (31A; 31B) and via which a monitoring signal is transmitted from an output to an input of the monitoring unit (10A; 10B). According to the invention, the monitoring signal is in the form of a sequence of pulses.

title: Method and apparatus for detecting the authenticity of the bank notes or in machines for dispensing objetssimilaires or changes
abstract: 1,179,483. Checking notes such as banknotes. K.G.R. SODERSTROM. April 17, 1967 [May 2, 1966; March 31, 1967], No.17496/67. Heading G1M. A method and apparatus for checking banknotes and for passing genuine undamaged notes to an apparatus for dispensing items and changing notes to coins comprises positioning a banknote in a checking station 7, gauging the dimension of at least one characterizing portion of the banknote, the values obtained being compared with standard values and/or measurement magnitudes at other portions of the banknote, as a result of which the forged or damaged notes are distinguished from the genuine undamaged ones, the genuine undamaged notes are passed to a place of collection and possibly start a dispensing apparatus and the forged and damaged notes are returned. The notes are fed through the apparatus by drive rolling 10 which in its operative position presses on roller 35. The note 21 is fed into the gauging apparatus through slot 40 passing under plungers 31, 341 having different surface areas which sink into the note by different amounts depending on the degree of uneveness, the plunger of smaller area plunging deepest. The difference in movement of the plungers with genuine undamaged notes should lie between certain limits e. g. the difference with smooth photographic paper is too small and with some forgeries is too great due to excessive roughness. The movement of the plungers 31, 341 is transmitted via leavers 28, 29 and 45, 46 to springs 61, 62 carrying contacts 65, 75 and 76, 77. If the banknote is a forgery contact is made over one or more of the contacts and the motor 17 is started in the reverse direction to return the note. If the banknote is genuine and undamaged the motor M continues in the same direction either to the dispencing apparatus or to a further gauging apparatus such as a photo-electric gauging mechanism 11, 19 for gauging the light transmission and light reflection of the banknote.(From GB1179483 A)

title: Method and apparatus for testing the focusing state of an electron beam for an electron beam welding process
abstract: 1,209,034. Automatic focus control. WELDING INSTITUTE. April 22, 1968 [April 25, 1967; Nov.20, 1967], Nos. 19062/67 and 52726/67. Heading G3R. [Also in Division H1] Focusing of the beam in an electron beam welding apparatus is connected automatically in response to signals from at least one probe which periodically intercepts the beam. In Fig. 1 three probes 13 are supported by a rod 12 from a shaft 10 driven by a motor so that the probes intercept the electron beam (not shown) once each revolution. The output current from the probes when the probes are staggered both horizontally and vertically as shown comprises three pulses Fig. 3 (not shown) the width of which corresponds to the width of the beam at the respective probes and the amplitude of which corresponds to the intensity of the beam. In an alternative arrangement, Fig.2 (not shown), the probes are stationary and the beam is scanned over them. In a modification of this arrangement, Figs.4 and 5 (not shown), the beam is periodically scanned along the boundaries of a quadrant thereby making two passes over an L-shaped probe. The output signals are used to provide automatic control of the current in a focusing coil, and in one arrangement, Fig. 6 (not shown), the peak voltage at each sweep is applied to a maximum voltage sensing device which senses a change of polarity in the slope of the signal resulting from the succession of peak voltages; whenever the polarity changes a signal is applied to a focus servo to adjust the coil current in the required direction. Alternatively the peak voltage may be applied to a null balance servo fed with a reference voltage. The probes are preferably ribbons placed edge on to the beam and may be of tungsten, copper or platinum.(From GB1209034 A)

title: Method and arrangement for monitoring connections in a program-controlled processing system, in particular in a program-controlled switching system
abstract: A method and apparatus for monitoring system connection units in program controlled telecommunications exchange systems to determine which units are producing connection requirements is described. Incoming and outgoing connections are identified over input and output code transducers. A storage cell in the central memory is permanently assigned to each incoming connection, and this storage cell can be accessed on the basis of the identification process carried on in the input code transducer. An operating cycle is simultaneously requested, and the system connecting unit generating a requirement is interrogated. The address of the system connection unit producing a request is identified and placed in a first address store. The address of an immediately preceding request is placed in a second address store. The contents of the two stores are compared, and in case of lack of identity the address in the first store is transferred to the second store. If identity is determined, an indication thereof is forwarded to a store for continuous requirements, and this causes the production of a signal for blocking the inputs to the second address store. A second comparison process then takes place between the address in the second address store and the addresses which are assigned to the succeeding connection requests. In case of a determination of identity in this second comparison process the connection requirement is blocked from being forwarded to the transmission sequence control and an advancing signal arrives at the input code converter.(From [publication reference] A)

title: Method and device for transmitting information
abstract: 1,108,804. Electric digital calculators. INTERNATIONAL BUSINESS MACHINES CORPORATION. 29 March, 1965 [6 April, 1964], No. 13160/65. Heading G4A. In a data processing system, input/output units are controlled in response to respective stored unit control words. A micro-programme-controlled central processing unit (CPU) can communicate with a selected input/output (I/O) unit over a common set of lines comprising two sets of nine lines (for an 8-bit byte and a parity bit) called " bus out " and " bus in," and in and out lines for indicating the presence on the corresponding bus of data (in or out), commands (out), addresses (in or out) or status information (in). Lines are provided to carry timing signals from the CPU to the I/O units. A " select out " line carries a signal from the CPU to the I/O units in turn in priority order. If an I/O unit does not require service it passes the signal to the next I/O unit, otherwise it blocks the signal and sends its address to the CPU to interrupt the current programme, the address indicating the identity of the I/O unit and the operation required. The far end of the " select out " line is connected to a " select in " line returning to the CPU. An " operational in " line is provided to indicate to the CPU that an I/O unit has been selected, and an " operational out " line is provided for interlocking purposes. A " suppress interrupt " (out) line is provided to enable the CPU to prevent the I/O units from interrupting it. The CPU may select a particular I/O unit by sending its address. I/O devices may be time-division multiplexed on to the set of lines to the CPU. The CPU memory stores I/O control words as follows: (a) channel command words CCW, (b) unit control words UCW, (c) channel status words CSW. A CCW has operation, count, flag and data address fields. The data address field gives the first byte address in CPU memory to be used for I/O operations, and the count field gives the number of consecutive byte locations after it which are available. The flag field comprises indications whether or not (a) addresses are to be chained (i.e. the storage area defined by the next CCW is to be used for the current operation), (b) commands are to be chained (i.e. the operation specified by the next CCW is to be performed with the present I/O unit), (e) data from the I/O unit is to be stored in the CPU memory, (d) the programme is to be interrupted. During an I/O operation, fields from the appropriate CCW are transferred to a UCW read from memory. A UCW has similar fields to a CCW, plus a status (of I/O unit) field and a field specifying the address of the next CCW. I/O control words are updated as necessary. An I/O device is disconnected, once selected, by a signal on the " address out " line without one on the " select out " line.(From GB1108804 A)
